translations.idiomatic: Volume 215

sentences.zh: 【唐紀三十一】 起玄黓敦牂，盡強圉大淵獻十一月，凡五年有奇。

translations.literal: [Tang Records 31] Beginning in the year Xuanji Dunzang, ending in the eleventh month of the year Qiangyu Dayuanxian; in all a little more than five years.
translations.idiomatic: [Tang Records 31] From 742 through the eleventh month of 746—a span of somewhat more than five years.

sentences.zh: 玄宗至道大聖大明孝皇帝中之下天寶元年（

translations.literal: The middle and lower portion of the reign of Emperor Xuanzong, Sagacious Emperor of the Supreme Way, Great Brightness, and Filial Piety—Tianbao year 1 (
translations.idiomatic: Middle and late reign of Emperor Xuanzong of the Tang—Tianbao, year 1 (

sentences.zh: 壬午，公元七四二年）

translations.literal: renwu, corresponding to the year 742 CE)
translations.idiomatic: CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，丁未朔，上御勤政樓受朝賀，赦天下，改元。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the day dingwei, the first of the month, the emperor ascended the Qinzheng Tower to receive court congratulations, pardoned all under Heaven, and changed the reign title.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the first day of the first month, the emperor went up to the Qinzheng Tower to receive the New Year court, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name.

sentences.zh: 壬子，分平盧別為節度，以安祿山為節度使。

translations.literal: On the day renzi, Pinglu was separated and made a distinct circuit; An Lushan was appointed its military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi day, Pinglu was split off as a separate frontier command, and An Lushan was made its jiedushi.

sentences.zh: 是時，天下聲教所被之州三百三十一，羈縻之州八百，置十節度、經略使以備邊。

translations.literal: At this time, throughout the realm there were 331 prefectures reached by the transforming influence of civilization and 800 suzerain prefectures; ten frontier commands and pacification commissioners were established to guard the borders.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the empire had 331 regular prefectures and 800 suzerain prefectures; ten frontier commands and pacification commissioners were set up to defend the borders.

sentences.zh: 安西節度撫寧西域，統龜茲、焉耆、于闐、疏勒四鎮，治龜茲城，兵二萬四千。

translations.literal: The Anxi command pacified and settled the Western Regions, controlling the four garrisons of Kucha, Karashahr, Khotan, and Kashgar; its seat was at Kucha city, with 24,000 troops.
translations.idiomatic: The Anxi command pacified the Western Regions and oversaw the four garrisons of Kucha, Karashahr, Khotan, and Kashgar, headquartered at Kucha with 24,000 soldiers.

sentences.zh: 北庭節度防制突騎施、堅昆，統瀚海、天山、伊吾三軍，屯伊、西二州之境，治北庭都護府，兵二萬人。

translations.literal: The Beiting command defended against the Turgesh and Kyrgyz, commanding the Hanhai, Tianshan, and Yiwu armies; it was stationed in the territories of Yi and Xi prefectures, with its seat at the Beiting Protectorate, and had 20,000 troops.
translations.idiomatic: The Beiting command held the Turgesh and Kyrgyz in check, commanding the Hanhai, Tianshan, and Yiwu armies in Yi and Xi prefectures from the Beiting Protectorate with 20,000 men.

sentences.zh: 河西節度斷隔吐蕃、突厥，統赤水、大斗、建康、寧寇、玉門、黑離、豆盧、新泉八軍，張掖、交城、白亭三守捉，屯涼、肅、瓜、沙、會五州之境，治涼州，兵七萬三千人。

translations.literal: The Hexi command cut off Tibetans and Turks, commanding eight armies—Chishui, Dadou, Jiankang, Ningkou, Yumen, Heili, Doulu, and Xinquan—and three defense posts at Zhangye, Jiaocheng, and Baiting; it was stationed in Liang, Su, Guazhou, Shazhou, and Hui prefectures, with its seat at Liangzhou, and had 73,000 troops.
translations.idiomatic: The Hexi command blocked Tibetan and Turkic power, commanding eight armies and three defense posts across five prefectures from Liangzhou, with 73,000 troops.

sentences.zh: 朔方節度捍御突厥，統經略、豐安、定遠三軍，三受降城，安北、單于二都護府，屯靈、夏、豐三州之境，治靈州，兵六萬四千七百人。

translations.literal: The Shuofang command defended against the Turks, commanding the Jinglue, Feng'an, and Dingyuan armies, the three cities for receiving surrender, and the Anbei and Chanyu protectorates; it was stationed in Ling, Xia, and Feng prefectures, with its seat at Lingzhou, and had 64,700 troops.
translations.idiomatic: The Shuofang command guarded against the Turks from Lingzhou, commanding three armies, three surrender cities, and two protectorates across Ling, Xia, and Feng prefectures, with 64,700 troops.

sentences.zh: 河東節度與朔方掎角以御突厥，統天兵、大同、橫野、岢嵐四軍，雲中守捉，屯太原府忻、代、嵐三州之境，治太原府，兵五萬五千人。

translations.literal: The Hedong command, in mutual support with Shuofang to resist the Turks, commanded the Tianbing, Datong, Hengye, and Kelan armies and the Yunzhong defense post; it was stationed in Xin, Dai, and Lan prefectures of Taiyuan prefecture, with its seat at Taiyuan, and had 55,000 troops.
translations.idiomatic: The Hedong command worked in tandem with Shuofang against the Turks from Taiyuan, commanding four armies and the Yunzhong defense post in Xin, Dai, and Lan prefectures, with 55,000 troops.

sentences.zh: 范陽節度臨制奚、契丹，統經略、威武、清夷、靜塞、恆陽、北平、高陽、唐興、橫海九軍，屯幽、薊、媯、檀、易、恆、定、漠、滄九州之境，治幽州，兵九萬一千四百人。

translations.literal: The Fanyang command oversaw the Xi and Khitan, commanding nine armies—Jinglue, Weiwu, Qingyi, Jingsai, Hengyang, Beiping, Gaoyang, Tangxing, and Henghai; it was stationed in nine prefectures—You, Ji, Gui, Tan, Yi, Heng, Ding, Mo, and Cang—with its seat at Youzhou, and had 91,400 troops.
translations.idiomatic: The Fanyang command controlled the Xi and Khitan from Youzhou, commanding nine armies across nine northeastern prefectures with 91,400 troops.

sentences.zh: 平盧節度鎮撫室韋、靺鞨，統平盧、盧龍二軍，榆關守捉，安東都護府，屯營、平二州之境，治營州，兵三萬七千五百人。

translations.literal: The Pinglu command pacified the Shiwei and Mohe, commanding the Pinglu and Lulong armies, the Yuguan defense post, and the Andong Protectorate; it was stationed in Ying and Ping prefectures, with its seat at Yingzhou, and had 37,500 troops.
translations.idiomatic: The Pinglu command kept the Shiwei and Mohe in line from Yingzhou, commanding two armies, the Yuguan defense post, and the Andong Protectorate in Ying and Ping prefectures, with 37,500 troops.

sentences.zh: 隴右節度備御吐蕃，統臨洮、河源、白水、安人、振威、威戎、漠門、寧塞、積石、鎮西十軍，綏和、合川、平夷三守捉，屯鄯、廊、洮、河之境，治鄯州，兵七萬五千人。

translations.literal: The Longyou command prepared against the Tibetans, commanding ten armies—Lintao, Heyuan, Baishui, Anren, Zhenwei, Weirong, Momen, Ningsai, Jishi, and Zhenxi—and three defense posts at Suihe, Hechuan, and Pingyi; it was stationed in Shan, Lang, Tao, and He prefectures, with its seat at Shanzhou, and had 75,000 troops.
translations.idiomatic: The Longyou command guarded against Tibet from Shanzhou, commanding ten armies and three defense posts across Shan, Lang, Tao, and He prefectures, with 75,000 troops.

sentences.zh: 劍南節度西抗吐蕃，南撫蠻獠，統天寶、平戎、昆明、寧遠、澄川、南江六軍，屯益、翼、茂、當、巂、柘、松、維、恭、雅、黎、姚、悉十三州之境，治益州，兵三萬九百人。

translations.literal: The Jiannan command resisted the Tibetans in the west and pacified the southern barbarians, commanding six armies—Tianbao, Pingrong, Kunming, Ningyuan, Chengchuan, and Nanjiang; it was stationed in thirteen prefectures—Yi, Yi, Mao, Dang, Xi, Zhe, Song, Wei, Gong, Ya, Li, Yao, and Xi—with its seat at Yizhou, and had 39,900 troops.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiannan command fought Tibet in the west and pacified southern tribes, commanding six armies across thirteen prefectures from Yizhou with 39,900 troops.

sentences.zh: 嶺南五府經略綏靜夷、獠，統經略、清海二軍，桂、容、邕、交四管，治廣州，兵萬五千四百人。

translations.literal: The Lingnan Five-Circuit Pacification Commission pacified the Yi and Liao peoples, commanding the Jinglue and Qinghai armies and four supervisory circuits—Gui, Rong, Yong, and Jiao; its seat was at Guangzhou, with 15,400 troops.
translations.idiomatic: The Lingnan pacification commissioner quieted the Yi and Liao, commanding two armies and four circuits from Guangzhou with 15,400 troops.

sentences.zh: 此外又有長樂經略，福州領之，兵千五百人。

translations.literal: Besides these there was also the Changle Pacification Commission, administered by Fuzhou, with 1,500 troops.
translations.idiomatic: There was also the Changle pacification commission under Fuzhou, with 1,500 troops.

sentences.zh: 東萊守捉，萊州領之；

translations.literal: The Donglai defense post was administered by Laizhou;
translations.idiomatic: The Donglai defense post was under Laizhou;

sentences.zh: 東牟守捉，登州領之；

translations.literal: the Dongmou defense post was administered by Dengzhou;
translations.idiomatic: the Dongmou defense post was under Dengzhou;

sentences.zh: 兵各千人。

translations.literal: each with 1,000 troops.
translations.idiomatic: each with a thousand men.

sentences.zh: 凡鎮兵四十九萬人，馬八萬餘匹。

translations.literal: In all there were 490,000 frontier troops and more than 80,000 horses.
translations.idiomatic: In all the frontier armies numbered 490,000 men and more than 80,000 horses.

sentences.zh: 開元之前，每歲供邊兵衣糧，費不過二百萬；

translations.literal: Before the Kaiyuan era, the annual cost of clothing and grain for frontier troops did not exceed 2 million;
translations.idiomatic: Before Kaiyuan, clothing and grain for the frontier armies cost no more than two million a year;

sentences.zh: 天寶之後，邊將奏益兵浸多，每歲用衣千二十萬匹，糧百九十萬斛，公私勞費，民始困苦矣。

translations.literal: after Tianbao, frontier generals memorialized for ever more troops; each year 10.2 million bolts of cloth and 1.9 million hu of grain were used, and with the labor and expense borne by public and private alike, the people began to suffer hardship.
translations.idiomatic: but after Tianbao the frontier generals kept requesting more troops until the annual cost reached 10.2 million bolts of cloth and 1.9 million hu of grain; public and private resources were strained, and the people grew distressed.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，陳王府參軍田同秀上言：「見玄元皇帝於丹鳳門之空中，告以『我藏靈符，在尹喜故宅。』」

translations.literal: On the day jiayin, Tian Tongxiu, adjutant of the Princely Establishment of Chen, memorialized: "I saw the Mysterious Origin Emperor in the air above the Danfeng Gate; he told me, 'I have hidden a numinous talisman in the former residence of Yin Xi.'"
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin day, Tian Tongxiu, adjutant of the Prince of Chen's household, reported: "I saw the Mysterious Origin Emperor in the sky above the Danfeng Gate. He said, 'I have hidden a sacred talisman in Yin Xi's old home.'"

sentences.zh: 上遣使於故函谷關尹喜台旁求得之。

translations.literal: The emperor sent envoys to search beside the Yin Xi terrace at the old Hangu Pass and obtained it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent men to the old Hangu Pass, searched beside Yin Xi's terrace, and found it.

sentences.zh: 陝州刺史李齊物穿三門運渠，辛未，渠成。

translations.literal: Li Qiwu, prefect of Shan prefecture, cut the transport canal at Sanmen; on the day xinwei the canal was completed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qiwu, prefect of Shan, cut a transport canal at Sanmen; on xinwei day the canal was finished.

sentences.zh: 齊物，神通之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Qiwu was a great-grandson of Li Shentong.
translations.idiomatic: Qiwu was the great-grandson of Li Shentong.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，群臣上表，以「函谷寶符，潛應年號；

translations.literal: On the day renchen, the officials submitted a memorial stating, "The precious talisman of Hangu secretly corresponds to the reign title;
translations.idiomatic: On renchen day the officials submitted a memorial: "The Hangu talisman secretly matches the reign title;

sentences.zh: 先天不違，請於尊號加『天寶』字。」

translations.literal: it does not violate the former title Xiantian—we request that the characters 'Tianbao' be added to the honorific title."
translations.idiomatic: it accords with Xiantian. We ask that the honorific title include the words 'Heavenly Treasure.'"

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 二月，辛卯，上享玄元皇帝於新廟。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the day xinmao, the emperor offered sacrifice to the Mysterious Origin Emperor at the new temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on xinmao day, the emperor sacrificed to the Mysterious Origin Emperor in the new temple.

sentences.zh: 甲午，享太廟。

translations.literal: On the day jiawu, he offered sacrifice at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu day he sacrificed at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 丙申，合祀天地於南郊，赦天下。

translations.literal: On the day bingshen, he performed the joint sacrifice to Heaven and Earth at the southern suburb and pardoned all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen day he offered the joint sacrifice to Heaven and Earth at the southern suburb and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 改侍中為左相，中書令為右相，尚書左、右丞相復為僕射；

translations.literal: He changed Shizhong to Left Chancellor, Zhongshu Ling to Right Chancellor, and restored the titles of Left and Right Directors of the Department of State Affairs to Pushe;
translations.idiomatic: He renamed Shizhong as Left Chancellor and Zhongshu Ling as Right Chancellor, and restored the titles of the heads of the Department of State Affairs to Pushe;

sentences.zh: 東都、北都皆為京，州為郡，刺史為太守；

translations.literal: both the Eastern and Northern Capitals were made imperial capitals, prefectures were called commanderies, and prefects were called grand administrators;
translations.idiomatic: both the Eastern and Northern Capitals were elevated to imperial capitals, prefectures became commanderies, and prefects became grand administrators;

sentences.zh: 改桃林縣曰靈寶。

translations.literal: and Taolin county was renamed Lingbao.
translations.idiomatic: and Taolin County was renamed Lingbao.

sentences.zh: 田同秀除朝散大夫。

translations.literal: Tian Tongxiu was appointed Chaosan Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Tongxiu was appointed Grand Master of Palace Attendance.

sentences.zh: 時人皆疑寶符同秀所為。

translations.literal: People at the time all suspected that the precious talisman had been fabricated by Tongxiu.
translations.idiomatic: At the time many suspected Tongxiu had forged the talisman himself.

sentences.zh: 間一歲，清河人崔以清復言：「見玄元皇帝於天津橋北，雲藏符在武城紫微山。」

translations.literal: A year later, Cui Yiqing of Qinghe again reported: "I saw the Mysterious Origin Emperor north of the Tianjin Bridge; he said the hidden talisman was on Mount Ziwei in Wucheng."
translations.idiomatic: A year later Cui Yiqing of Qinghe reported again: "I saw the Mysterious Origin Emperor north of the Tianjin Bridge. He said a talisman was hidden on Mount Ziwei in Wucheng."

sentences.zh: 敕使往掘，亦得之。

translations.literal: Imperial envoys were sent to dig, and it too was found.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent men to dig there, and they found one as well.

sentences.zh: 東京留守王倕知其詐，按問，果首服。

translations.literal: Wang Yun, regent of the Eastern Capital, knew it was a fraud; upon investigation, the culprits indeed confessed first.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yun, regent of the Eastern Capital, saw through the fraud; when he investigated, the men confessed at once.

sentences.zh: 奏之。

translations.literal: He reported this.
translations.idiomatic: He reported it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 上亦不深罪，流之而已。

translations.literal: The emperor did not punish them severely, merely exiling them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not punish them harshly and merely had them exiled.

sentences.zh: 三月，以長安令韋堅為陝郡太守，領江、淮租庸轉運使。

translations.literal: In the third month, Wei Jian, magistrate of Chang'an, was appointed Grand Administrator of Shan commandery and made commissioner for transport of Jiang-Huai rent and corvée.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Wei Jian, magistrate of Chang'an, was made grand administrator of Shan commandery and commissioner for Jiang-Huai grain transport.

sentences.zh: 初，宇文融既敗，言利者稍息。

translations.literal: Earlier, after Yuwen Rong's fall, those who spoke of profit-making gradually fell silent.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Yuwen Rong's downfall, talk of profit-seeking had largely subsided.

sentences.zh: 及楊慎矜得幸，於是韋堅、王□之徒競以利進，百司有事權者，稍稍別置使以領之，舊官充位而已。

translations.literal: When Yang Shenjin gained favor, then Wei Jian, Wang Yue, and their like all competed to advance through profit-making; in every office that held real power, special commissioners were gradually set up to take charge, while the old officials merely filled their posts in name.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Shenjin won the emperor's favor, Wei Jian, Wang Yue, and others vied to rise by promising revenue. Offices with real power gradually set up special commissioners to run things, while the old officials held empty titles.

sentences.zh: 堅，太子之妃兄也，為吏以干敏稱。

translations.literal: Jian was the elder brother of the crown prince's consort and was known as an official for his resourcefulness and keenness.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was the crown prince's brother-in-law and was known as a capable, quick-witted official.

sentences.zh: 上使之督江、淮租運，歲增巨萬；

translations.literal: The emperor had him supervise Jiang-Huai rent transport, and each year the revenue increased by tens of thousands;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor put him in charge of Jiang-Huai transport, and revenue increased by tens of thousands each year;

sentences.zh: 上以為能，故擢任之。

translations.literal: the emperor considered him capable and therefore promoted him.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor judged him capable and promoted him accordingly.

sentences.zh: 王□，方翼之孫也，亦以善治租賦為戶部員外郎兼侍御史。

translations.literal: Wang Yue was a grandson of Wang Fangyi and, also for skill in managing rent and taxes, served as Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue and concurrently as Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yue, grandson of Wang Fangyi, likewise became vice director in the Ministry of Revenue and attending censor for his skill in managing taxes.

sentences.zh: 李林甫為相，凡才望功業出己右及為上所厚、勢位將逼己者，必百計去之；

translations.literal: As chief minister, Li Linfu invariably removed by every stratagem anyone whose talent, reputation, or achievements surpassed his own, anyone whom the emperor favored, or anyone whose position and power threatened to press upon him;
translations.idiomatic: As chief minister, Li Linfu removed by every means anyone more talented, accomplished, or favored than himself, or anyone whose power threatened his own;

sentences.zh: 尤忌文學之士，或陽與之善，啖以甘言而陰陷之。

translations.literal: he especially hated men of literary talent, and would sometimes feign friendship with them, feeding them sweet words while secretly entrapping them.
translations.idiomatic: he especially hated literary men and would sometimes feign friendship, speak honeyed words, and ruin them in secret.

sentences.zh: 世謂李林甫「口有蜜，腹有劍。」

translations.literal: The age said of Li Linfu, "Honey in the mouth, a sword in the belly."
translations.idiomatic: People said of Li Linfu, "Honey on the lips, a sword in the belly."

sentences.zh: 上嘗陳樂於勤政樓下，垂簾觀之。

translations.literal: The emperor once had music performed below the Qinzheng Tower and watched from behind a lowered curtain.
translations.idiomatic: Once the emperor had music performed below the Qinzheng Tower and watched from behind a lowered curtain.

sentences.zh: 兵部侍郎盧絢謂上已起，垂鞭按轡，橫過樓下；

translations.literal: Lu Xuan, Vice Director of the Ministry of War, thinking the emperor had already risen, let his whip hang and held his reins as he rode across below the tower;
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xuan, vice director of the Ministry of War, thinking the emperor had already left, rode across below the tower with whip lowered and reins in hand;

sentences.zh: 絢風標清粹，上目送之；

translations.literal: Xuan's bearing was pure and refined, and the emperor followed him with his eyes;
translations.idiomatic: Xuan had a refined bearing, and the emperor watched him go;

sentences.zh: 深歎其蘊藉。

translations.literal: deeply admiring his cultivated restraint.
translations.idiomatic: deeply admiring his cultivated ease.

sentences.zh: 林甫常厚以金帛賂上左右，上舉動必知之；

translations.literal: Linfu regularly lavished gold and silk on those close to the emperor, so that he always knew the emperor's every move;
translations.idiomatic: Linfu regularly bribed the emperor's attendants with gold and silk and always knew the emperor's every move;

sentences.zh: 乃召絢子弟謂曰：「尊君素望清崇，今交、廣藉才，聖上欲以尊君為之，可乎？

translations.literal: he then summoned Xuan's sons and told them, "Your father's reputation has long been lofty and pure. Jiao and Guang now need talent, and His Majesty wishes to appoint your father there. Would that be acceptable?
translations.idiomatic: then summoned Xuan's sons and said, "Your father has long enjoyed a lofty reputation. Jiao and Guang need talent now, and His Majesty wishes to appoint him there. Would that be acceptable?

sentences.zh: 若憚遠行，則當左遷；

translations.literal: If he fears the long journey, he will be demoted instead;
translations.idiomatic: If he fears the long journey, he will be demoted instead;

sentences.zh: 不然，以賓、詹分務東洛，亦優賢之命也，何如？」

translations.literal: otherwise, to serve in the Eastern Capital as Guest of the Crown Prince and Junior Mentor while sharing duties—that too is an honorable appointment for the worthy. What do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: otherwise, to serve in the Eastern Capital as guest of the crown prince and junior mentor while sharing duties—that too is an honorable post for a worthy man. What do you think?"

sentences.zh: 絢懼，以賓、詹為請。

translations.literal: Xuan, in fear, requested the posts of Guest and Junior Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Xuan asked for the guest and junior mentor posts.

sentences.zh: 林甫恐乖眾望，乃除華州刺史。

translations.literal: Linfu, fearing to go against public expectation, then appointed him Prefect of Hua.
translations.idiomatic: Linfu, fearing public backlash, then appointed him prefect of Hua.

sentences.zh: 到官未幾，誣其有疾，州事不理，除詹事、員外同正。

translations.literal: Shortly after he took office, Linfu falsely claimed he was ill and neglected prefectural affairs; he was appointed Mentor of the Heir Apparent with the additional title of Regular Attendant Outside the Regular Establishment.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he took office, Linfu claimed he was ill and neglected his duties; he was made mentor of the heir apparent with an honorary attendant title.

sentences.zh: 上又嘗問林甫以「嚴挺之今安在？

translations.literal: The emperor also once asked Linfu, "Where is Yan Tingzhi now?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also once asked Linfu, "Where is Yan Tingzhi now?

sentences.zh: 是人亦可用。」

translations.literal: This man too may be employed."
translations.idiomatic: That man could also be used."

sentences.zh: 挺之時為絳州刺史。

translations.literal: At the time Tingzhi was Prefect of Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Tingzhi was prefect of Jiang.

sentences.zh: 林甫退，召挺之弟損之，諭以「上待尊兄意甚厚，盍為見上之策，奏稱風疾，求還京師就醫。」

translations.literal: Linfu withdrew and summoned Tingzhi's younger brother Sunzhi, instructing him, "His Majesty's regard for your elder brother is very deep. Why not devise a plan to see the emperor—memorialize that he suffers from wind ailment and ask to return to the capital for treatment?"
translations.idiomatic: Linfu withdrew and summoned Tingzhi's younger brother Sunzhi. "The emperor thinks highly of your brother," he said. "Why not have him memorialize that he has a wind ailment and ask to return to the capital for treatment?"

sentences.zh: 挺之從之。

translations.literal: Tingzhi complied.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhi did so.

sentences.zh: 林甫以其奏白上云：「挺之衰老得風疾，宜且授以散秩，使便醫藥。」

translations.literal: Linfu reported his memorial to the emperor, saying, "Tingzhi is aged and has contracted wind ailment; he should be given a nominal rank for the time being so that he may conveniently take medicine."
translations.idiomatic: Linfu reported the memorial to the emperor: "Tingzhi is old and has a wind ailment. He should be given an honorary post for now so he can receive treatment."

sentences.zh: 上歎吒久之；

translations.literal: The emperor sighed for a long while;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed for a long time;

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，壬寅，以為詹事，又以汴州刺史、河南採訪使齊澣為少詹事，皆員外同正，於東京養疾。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the day renyin, he was appointed Mentor of the Heir Apparent, and Qi Huan, Prefect of Bian and Henan Investigation Commissioner, was appointed Junior Mentor; both held the additional title of Regular Attendant Outside the Regular Establishment and were to convalesce in the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on renyin day, he was made mentor of the heir apparent, and Qi Huan, prefect of Bian and Henan investigation commissioner, was made junior mentor; both received honorary attendant titles and were to convalesce in the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 澣亦朝廷宿望，故並忌之。

translations.literal: Huan too was a man of long-standing repute at court, and therefore Linfu envied them both.
translations.idiomatic: Huan was also a man of long standing at court, and Linfu envied them both.

sentences.zh: 上發兵納十姓可汗阿史那昕於突騎施，至俱蘭城，為莫賀達干所殺。

translations.literal: The emperor sent troops to install Ashina Xin of the Ten Surnames as khan among the Turgesh; when they reached Julan city, he was killed by Mohedagan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent troops to install Ashina Xin of the Ten Surnames among the Turgesh; at Julan city he was killed by Mohedagan.

sentences.zh: 突騎施大纛官都摩度來降，六月，乙未，冊都摩度為三姓葉護。

translations.literal: Dumodu, the great-banner officer of the Turgesh, came to surrender; in the sixth month, on the day yiwei, Dumodu was enfeoffed as Yabghu of the Three Surnames.
translations.idiomatic: Dumodu, the Turgesh great-banner officer, surrendered; in the sixth month, on yiwei day, he was enfeoffed as yabghu of the Three Surnames.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，癸卯朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the first day guimao, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, on the first day of the seventh month, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 辛未，左相牛仙客薨。

translations.literal: On the day xinwei, Left Chancellor Niu Xianke died.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei day Left Chancellor Niu Xianke died.

sentences.zh: 八月，丁丑，以刑部尚書李適之為左相。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the day dingchou, Li Shizhi, Minister of Justice, was appointed Left Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on dingchou day, Li Shizhi, minister of justice, was made left chancellor.

sentences.zh: 突厥拔悉蜜、回紇、葛邏祿三部共攻骨咄葉護，殺之，推拔悉蜜酋長為頡跌伊施可汗，回紇、葛邏祿自為左、右葉護。

translations.literal: The three Turkic tribes of Basmyl, Uyghur, and Karluk jointly attacked the Yabghu Kutlug and killed him; they installed the Basmyl chieftain as Irdaš Iš Qaghan, while the Uyghurs and Karluk made themselves Left and Right Yabghu respectively.
translations.idiomatic: The Basmyl, Uyghur, and Karluk tribes jointly attacked and killed Yabghu Kutlug, installed the Basmyl chieftain as Irdaš Iš Qaghan, and made themselves left and right yabghu.

sentences.zh: 突厥餘眾共立判闕特勒之子為烏蘇米施可汗，以其子葛臘哆為西殺。

translations.literal: The remaining Turks jointly installed the son of Panjue Tegin as Qaghan Wu-su-mi-shi, and appointed his son Geladuo as Western Shad.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining Turks installed the son of Panjue Tegin as Qaghan Wu-su-mi-shi and appointed his son Geladuo as western shad.

sentences.zh: 上遣使諭烏蘇令內附，烏蘇不從。

translations.literal: The emperor sent envoys to instruct Wu-su to submit and come within the borders; Wu-su refused.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent envoys urging Wu-su to submit; Wu-su refused.

sentences.zh: 朔方節度使王忠嗣盛兵磧口以威之，烏蘇懼，請降，而遷延不至。

translations.literal: Wang Zhongsi, military commissioner of Shuofang, massed troops at Qikou to overawe him; Wu-su grew afraid and requested surrender, but delayed and did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhongsi, Shuofang military commissioner, massed troops at Qikou to intimidate him; Wu-su grew afraid and asked to surrender but kept delaying.

sentences.zh: 忠嗣知其詐，乃遣使說拔悉蜜、回紇、葛邏祿使攻之，烏蘇遁去。

translations.literal: Zhongsi knew this was deceit and therefore sent envoys to persuade the Basmyl, Uyghurs, and Karluk to attack him; Wu-su fled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongsi saw through the ruse and sent envoys to persuade the Basmyl, Uyghurs, and Karluk to attack; Wu-su fled.

sentences.zh: 忠嗣因出兵擊之，取其右廂以歸。

translations.literal: Zhongsi then led troops in pursuit, took his right wing, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongsi then attacked, captured his right wing, and returned.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，突厥西葉護阿布思及西殺葛臘哆、默啜之孫勃德支、伊然小妻、毘伽登利之女帥部眾千餘帳，相次來降，突厥遂微。

translations.literal: On the day dinghai, the Turkic Western Yabghu Abu Si, the Western Shad Geladuo, Bodezhi grandson of Mo-ch'o, Yiran the junior consort, and the daughter of Bilge Qaghan Dengli led more than a thousand yurts of their tribesmen to surrender in succession, and the Turks thereafter grew weak.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai day the Turkic western yabghu Abu Si, western shad Geladuo, Mo-ch'o's grandson Bodezhi, junior consort Yiran, and Bilge Qaghan Dengli's daughter led more than a thousand yurts to surrender in succession, and Turkish power waned.

sentences.zh: 九月，辛亥，上御花萼樓宴突厥降者，賞賜甚厚。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the day xinhai, the emperor ascended the Hua'e Tower to feast the surrendering Turks and rewarded them very generously.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on xinhai day, the emperor feasted the surrendering Turks at the Hua'e Tower and rewarded them lavishly.

sentences.zh: 護密先附吐蕃，戊午，其王頡吉裡匐遣使請降。

translations.literal: Humi had earlier submitted to Tibet; on the day wuwu, its king Fazang dispatched envoys to request surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Humi had earlier sided with Tibet; on wuwu day its king Fazang sent envoys to surrender.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丁酉，上幸驪山溫泉；

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the day dingyou, the emperor visited the hot springs at Mount Li;
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on dingyou day, the emperor went to the hot springs at Mount Li;

sentences.zh: 己巳，還宮。

translations.literal: on the day jisi, he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: on jisi day he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 十二月，隴右節度使皇甫惟明奏破吐蕃大嶺等軍；

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Huangfu Weiming, military commissioner of Longyou, memorialized that he had defeated the Tibetan armies of Daling and others;
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Huangfu Weiming, Longyou military commissioner, reported defeating the Tibetan armies of Daling and others;

sentences.zh: 戊戌，又奏破青海道莽布支營三萬餘眾，斬獲五千餘級。

translations.literal: on the day wuxu, he further memorialized that he had defeated more than 30,000 men in the camp of Mangbuje on the Qinghai route, killing and capturing more than 5,000.
translations.idiomatic: on wuxu day he further reported defeating more than 30,000 men in Mangbuje's camp on the Qinghai route, killing and capturing more than 5,000.

sentences.zh: 庚子，河西節度使王倕奏破吐蕃漁海及游弈等軍。

translations.literal: On the day gengzi, Wang Yun, military commissioner of Hexi, memorialized that he had defeated the Tibetan armies of Yuhai and Youyi.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi day Wang Yun, Hexi military commissioner, reported defeating the Tibetan armies of Yuhai and Youyi.

sentences.zh: 是歲，天下縣一千五百二十八，鄉一萬六千八百二十九，戶八百五十二萬五千七百六十三，口四千八百九十萬九千八百。

translations.literal: That year, throughout the realm there were 1,528 counties, 16,829 townships, 8,525,763 households, and 48,909,800 persons.
translations.idiomatic: That year the empire had 1,528 counties, 16,829 townships, 8,525,763 households, and a population of 48,909,800.

sentences.zh: 回紇葉護骨力裴羅遣使入貢，賜爵奉義王。

translations.literal: Kutlug Bilge Qutlugh Qutlugh, Yabghu of the Uyghurs, sent envoys to offer tribute and was granted the title Prince Who Upholds Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Kutlug Bilge, Uyghur yabghu, sent tribute envoys and was granted the title Prince Who Upholds Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 玄宗至道大聖大明孝皇帝中之下天寶二年（

translations.literal: The middle and lower portion of the reign of Emperor Xuanzong, Sagacious Emperor of the Supreme Way, Great Brightness, and Filial Piety—Tianbao year 2 (
translations.idiomatic: Middle and late reign of Emperor Xuanzong of the Tang—Tianbao, year 2 (

sentences.zh: 癸未，公元七四三年）

translations.literal: guiwei, corresponding to the year 743 CE)
translations.idiomatic: CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，安祿山入朝；

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, An Lushan came to court;
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, An Lushan came to court;

sentences.zh: 上寵待甚厚，謁見無時。

translations.literal: The emperor favored and treated him very generously; he could be received in audience at any time without restriction.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor showered him with favor and allowed him to attend audience at any hour.

sentences.zh: 祿山奏言：「去秋營州蟲食苗，臣焚香祝天云：『臣若操心不正，事君不忠，願使蟲食臣心；

translations.literal: Lushan memorialized, saying, "Last autumn in Ying Prefecture insects ate the seedlings. Your subject burned incense and prayed to Heaven, saying, 'If your subject's heart is not upright and his service to his lord is not loyal, may the insects eat your subject's heart;
translations.idiomatic: Lushan memorialized: "Last autumn in Ying Prefecture insects devoured the crops. I burned incense and prayed to Heaven: 'If my heart is not upright and my service to my lord is not loyal, may the insects eat my heart;

sentences.zh: 若不負神祇，願使蟲散。』

translations.literal: if I have not failed the spirits, may the insects disperse.'"
translations.idiomatic: if I have not failed the spirits, may the insects disperse.'"

sentences.zh: 即有群鳥從北來，食蟲立盡。

translations.literal: Immediately a flock of birds came from the north and ate the insects until they were all gone.
translations.idiomatic: At once a flock of birds came from the north and devoured the insects in an instant.

sentences.zh: 請宣付史官。」

translations.literal: I request that this be proclaimed and handed to the historians."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that this be proclaimed and recorded by the historians."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 李林甫領吏部尚書，日在政府，選事悉委侍郎宋遙、苗晉卿。

translations.literal: Li Linfu held the post of Minister of Personnel and was daily at the Secretariat; all matters of selection he entirely entrusted to Vice Ministers Song Yao and Miao Jinqing.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu held the ministry of personnel and was at the secretariat every day; he entrusted all selections entirely to Vice Ministers Song Yao and Miao Jinqing.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞張倚新得幸於上，遙、晉卿欲附之。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Zhang Yi had recently won the emperor's favor, and Yao and Jinqing wished to attach themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Zhang Yi had recently won the emperor's favor, and Yao and Jinqing sought his patronage.

sentences.zh: 時選人集者以萬計，入等者六十四人。

translations.literal: At the time candidates assembled in numbers of tens of thousands; those who passed into the selected ranks were sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands of candidates had assembled; only sixty-four passed the selection.

sentences.zh: 倚子奭為之首，群議沸騰。

translations.literal: Yi's son Shi ranked first, and public talk seethed.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's son Shi ranked first, and public outrage erupted.

sentences.zh: 前薊令蘇孝韞以告安祿山，祿山入言於上，上悉召入等人面試之，奭手持試紙，終日不成一字，時人謂之「曳白」。

translations.literal: Former Ji Prefect Su Xiaoyun reported it to An Lushan; Lushan entered and spoke of it to the emperor. The emperor summoned all who had passed for a face-to-face examination. Shi held the examination paper in hand and throughout the day could not complete a single character. People of the time called this "dragging a blank."
translations.idiomatic: Former prefect of Ji Su Xiaoyun reported the affair to An Lushan, who brought it to the emperor. The emperor summoned all sixty-four passers for a personal examination. Shi held his paper all day and could not write a single character. People called it "dragging a blank sheet."

sentences.zh: 癸亥，遙貶武當太守，晉卿貶安康太守，倚貶淮陽太守，同考判官禮部郎中裴朏等皆貶嶺南官。

translations.literal: On the day guihai, Yao was demoted to Prefect of Wudang, Jinqing to Prefect of Ankang, Yi to Prefect of Huaiyang, and the co-examiners including Ministry of Rites Section Chief Pei Fei were all demoted to posts in Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai day, Yao was demoted to prefect of Wudang, Jinqing to prefect of Ankang, and Yi to prefect of Huaiyang; the co-examiners, including Ministry of Rites section chief Pei Fei, were all sent to posts in Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 晉卿，壺關人也。

translations.literal: Jinqing was a native of Huguan.
translations.idiomatic: Jinqing came from Huguan.

sentences.zh: 三月，壬子，追尊玄元皇帝父周上御大夫為先天太皇；

translations.literal: In the third month, on the day renzi, posthumously honored the father of the Profound Origin Emperor, Senior Grand Master of the Zhou court, as Prior Heaven Grand Emperor;
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on renzi day, the court posthumously honored the father of the Profound Origin Emperor, once senior grand master of Zhou, as Prior Heaven Grand Emperor;

sentences.zh: 又尊皋繇為德明皇帝，涼武昭王為興聖皇帝。

translations.literal: also posthumously honored Gao Yao as Virtuous Brightness Emperor and the Martial Enlightened King of Liang as Flourishing Sage Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: and also honored Gao Yao as Virtuous Brightness Emperor and the martial enlightened King of Liang as Flourishing Sage Emperor.

sentences.zh: 江、淮南租庸等使韋堅引滻水抵苑東望春樓下為潭，以聚江、淮運船，役夫匠通漕渠，發人丘壟，自江、淮至京城，民間蕭然愁怨，二年而成。

translations.literal: Wei Jian, commissioner for rent, corvée, and related duties in the Jiang and Huai regions, diverted the Chan River to form a pool below Wangchun Tower east of the gardens, to gather transport ships from the Jiang and Huai; he employed craftsmen to open the canal, conscripted men to raise embankments, and from the Jiang and Huai to the capital the common people were desolate with worry and resentment; in two years it was completed.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Jian, commissioner for Jiang and Huai rents and corvée, diverted the Chan River into a basin below Wangchun Tower east of the palace gardens to receive grain ships from the Jiang and Huai. He pressed laborers into opening canals and conscripted men for embankment work; from the Jiang and Huai to the capital, the people were left desolate and bitter. The project took two years.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，上幸望春樓觀新潭。

translations.literal: On the day bingyin, the emperor visited Wangchun Tower to view the new basin.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin day, the emperor visited Wangchun Tower to view the new basin.

sentences.zh: 堅以新船數百艘，扁榜郡名，各陳郡中珍貨於船背；

translations.literal: Jian had several hundred new ships, each bearing placards with the name of a commandery, and on the backs of each were displayed the precious goods of that commandery;
translations.idiomatic: Jian arrayed several hundred new ships, each labeled with a commandery name and displaying that region's finest goods on deck;

sentences.zh: 陝尉崔成甫著錦半臂，鈌胯綠衫而裼之，紅袹首，居前船唱《得寶歌》，使美婦百人盛飾而和之，連檣數里；

translations.literal: Shan Assistant Magistrate Cui Chengfu wore a brocade half-sleeve, green trousers with iron clasps and bared them, and a red kerchief on his head; he stood on the lead ship singing "Song of Obtaining Treasure," with a hundred beautifully adorned women harmonizing, and the ships stretched in a continuous line for several li;
translations.idiomatic: Shan assistant magistrate Cui Chengfu wore brocade half-sleeves, green trousers with iron clasps bared to the thigh, and a red headcloth; he stood on the lead ship singing "Song of Obtaining Treasure," while a hundred lavishly dressed women harmonized behind him, and the fleet stretched for miles.

sentences.zh: 堅跪進諸郡輕貨，仍上百牙盤食。

translations.literal: Jian knelt and presented the light goods of the various commanderies, and also offered a hundred dishes on tooth-pattern trays.
translations.idiomatic: Jian knelt to present the finest goods of each commandery and also offered a hundred dishes on elaborate trays.

sentences.zh: 上置宴，竟日而罷，觀者山積。

translations.literal: The emperor set out a feast; when the day ended it was dismissed, and spectators piled up like a mountain.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held a feast that lasted all day; the crowd of onlookers was immense.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，加堅左散騎常侍，其僚屬吏卒褒賞有差；

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Jian was promoted to Left Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, and his subordinates, clerks, and soldiers received rewards in differing degrees;
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, Jian was promoted to left regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, and his staff and laborers were rewarded in varying measure;

sentences.zh: 名其潭曰廣運。

translations.literal: the basin was named Broad Transport.
translations.idiomatic: and the basin was named Broad Transport.

sentences.zh: 時京兆尹韓朝宗亦引渭水置潭於西街，以貯材木。

translations.literal: At the time Metropolitan Prefect Han Chaozong also diverted the Wei River to set a basin on West Street for storing timber.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time Metropolitan Prefect Han Chaozong diverted the Wei to create a basin on West Street for storing lumber.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，皇甫惟明引軍出西平，擊吐蕃，行千餘里，攻洪濟城，破之。

translations.literal: On the day dinghai, Huangfu Weiming led troops out from Xiping, struck Tibet, marched more than a thousand li, attacked Hongji City, and broke it.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai day, Huangfu Weiming marched from Xiping against Tibet, advanced more than a thousand li, attacked Hongji City, and took it.

sentences.zh: 上以右贊善大夫楊慎矜知御史中丞事。

translations.literal: The emperor had Right Palace Companion Yang Shenjing oversee the duties of Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Right Palace Companion Yang Shenjing act as censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 時李林甫專權，公卿之進，有不出其門者，必以罪去之；

translations.literal: At the time Li Linfu monopolized power; of those ministers who advanced without coming through his gate, he invariably removed them on some charge;
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu monopolized power at the time; any minister who rose without his patronage was invariably removed on some charge.

sentences.zh: 慎矜由是固辭，不敢受。

translations.literal: Shenjing therefore firmly declined and did not dare accept.
translations.idiomatic: Shenjing firmly declined and would not accept the post.

sentences.zh: 五月，辛丑，以慎矜為諫議大夫。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the day xinchou, Shenjing was appointed Remonstrance Officer.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on xinchou day, Shenjing was made remonstrance officer.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，戊寅，上幸驪山溫泉；

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the day wuyin, the emperor visited Mount Li hot springs;
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on wuyin day, the emperor went to the hot springs at Mount Li;

sentences.zh: 乙卯，還宮。

translations.literal: On the day yimao, he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao day he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 玄宗至道大聖大明孝皇帝中之下天寶三年（

translations.literal: Middle-lower portion of the reign of Emperor Xuanzong, Sagacious Emperor of the Supreme Way, Great Brightness, and Filial Piety—Tianbao year 3 (
translations.idiomatic: Middle-lower portion of the reign of Emperor Xuanzong of the Tang—Tianbao year 3 (

sentences.zh: 甲申，公元七四四年）

translations.literal: jiashen, corresponding to the year 744 CE)
translations.idiomatic: jiashen, AD 744)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，丙申朔，改年曰載。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the first day of the month bingchen, the reign era was changed and named Zai.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on the new moon of bingchen day, the era name was changed to Zai.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，上幸驪山溫泉；

translations.literal: On the day xinchou, the emperor visited Mount Li hot springs;
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou day the emperor went to the Mount Li hot springs;

sentences.zh: 二月，庚午，還宮。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the day gengwu, he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on gengwu day, he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，太子更名亨。

translations.literal: On the day xinmao, the Crown Prince's name was changed to Heng.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao day the crown prince was renamed Heng.

sentences.zh: 海賊吳令光等抄掠台、明，命河南尹裴敦復將兵討之。

translations.literal: Sea bandits Wu Lingguang and others raided Tai and Ming; the emperor ordered Henan Prefect Pei Dunfu to lead troops to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Sea bandits led by Wu Lingguang raided Tai and Ming; the emperor ordered Henan prefect Pei Dunfu to lead troops against them.

sentences.zh: 三月，己巳，以平盧節度使安祿山兼范陽節度使；

translations.literal: In the third month, on the day jisi, An Lushan, military commissioner of Pinglu, was additionally made military commissioner of Fanyang;
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on jisi day, An Lushan, commissioner of Pinglu, was also made commissioner of Fanyang;

sentences.zh: 以范陽節度使裴寬為戶部尚書。

translations.literal: Pei Kuan, military commissioner of Fanyang, was appointed Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: and Pei Kuan, commissioner of Fanyang, was appointed minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書席建侯為河北黜陟使，稱祿山公直；

translations.literal: Minister of Rites Xi Jianhou served as Hebei review commissioner and praised Lushan as upright and fair;
translations.idiomatic: Minister of rites Xi Jianhou, sent as Hebei review commissioner, praised Lushan as upright;

sentences.zh: 李林甫、裴寬皆順旨稱其美。

translations.literal: Li Linfu and Pei Kuan both followed the intent of the throne and praised his merits.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu and Pei Kuan both flattered him to the emperor's satisfaction.

sentences.zh: 三人皆上所信任，由是祿山之寵益固不搖矣。

translations.literal: All three were men in whom the emperor placed trust; by this Lushan's favor grew still more firmly unshaken.
translations.idiomatic: All three men enjoyed the emperor's trust, and Lushan's favor grew unshakeable.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，裴敦復破吳令光，擒之。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Pei Dunfu defeated Wu Lingguang and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, Pei Dunfu defeated Wu Lingguang and took him prisoner.

sentences.zh: 五月，河西節度使夫蒙靈察討突騎施莫賀達干，斬之，更請立黑姓伊裡底蜜施骨咄祿毘伽；

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Hexi Military Commissioner Fumeng Lingcha campaigned against the Turgesh chief Mohadagan, beheaded him, and further requested that the Black-bone clan's Yili Di Mish Boneulu Pijia be established;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Hexi commissioner Fumeng Lingcha campaigned against the Turgesh chief Mohadagan, killed him, and asked that the Black Clan leader Yili Di Mish Boneulu Pijia be enthroned;

sentences.zh: 六月，甲辰，冊拜骨咄祿毘伽為十姓可汗。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day jiachen, Boneulu Pijia was invested and enfeoffed as Khan of the Ten Surnames.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on jiachen day, Boneulu Pijia was invested as khan of the Ten Surnames.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，拔悉蜜攻斬突厥烏蘇可汗，傳首京師。

translations.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, the Basmyl attacked and beheaded the Türk Khagan Wusu, and sent his head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the eighth month, the Basmyl killed the Türk khagan Wusu and sent his head to the capital.

sentences.zh: 國人立其弟鶻隴匐白眉特勒，是為白眉可汗。

translations.literal: The people of the state installed his younger brother Helongfu, the White-Eyebrow Tegin, who became the White-Eyebrow Khagan.
translations.idiomatic: The Türks installed his younger brother Helongfu as the White-Eyebrow Tegin, and he became the White-Eyebrow Khagan.

sentences.zh: 於是突厥大亂，敕朔方節度使王忠嗣出兵乘之。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Türks fell into great disorder; an edict ordered Shuofang Military Commissioner Wang Zhongsi to march out troops and seize the opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: The Türks fell into chaos, and the court ordered Shuofang commissioner Wang Zhongsi to march and exploit the disorder.

sentences.zh: 至薩河內山，破其左廂阿波達乾等十一部，右廂未下。

translations.literal: Reaching Mount Sahenei within the Sa River region, he broke the left wing's Apodagan and eleven other tribes; the right wing was not yet subdued.
translations.idiomatic: At Sahenei Mountain within the Sa River region he defeated the left wing's Apodagan and eleven other tribes; the right wing remained unconquered.

sentences.zh: 會回紇、葛邏祿共攻拔悉蜜頡跌伊施可汗，殺之。

translations.literal: At the same time the Uyghurs and Qarlugs jointly attacked and killed the Basmyl Khagan Yiedie Yishi.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the Uyghurs and Qarlugs jointly attacked and killed the Basmyl khagan Yiedie Yishi.

sentences.zh: 回紇骨力裴羅自立為骨咄祿毘伽闕可汗，遣使言狀；

translations.literal: The Uyghur Kul Bilge Külü set himself up as Boneulu Pijia Qaghan Khagan and sent envoys to report the situation;
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghur leader Kul Bilge Külü proclaimed himself Boneulu Pijia Qaghan Khagan and sent envoys to report;

sentences.zh: 上冊拜裴羅為懷仁可汗。

translations.literal: the emperor invested and enfeoffed Bilge as Huairan Khagan.
translations.idiomatic: and the emperor invested Bilge as Huairan Khagan.

sentences.zh: 於是懷仁南據突厥故地，立牙帳於烏德犍山，舊統藥邏葛等九姓，其後又並拔悉蜜、葛邏祿，凡十一部，各置都督，每戰則以二客部為先。

translations.literal: Thereupon Huairan seized the old Türk lands to the south and set up his royal encampment on Mount Wudejian; he had formerly ruled the nine surnames including the Yaghlakar, and afterward also annexed the Basmyl and Qarlugs, eleven tribes in all, each with a supervisory commander appointed; in every battle the two guest tribes went first.
translations.idiomatic: Huairan then held the old Türk lands in the south and established his court at Mount Wudejian. He had once ruled the nine tribes including the Yaghlakar; later he also absorbed the Basmyl and Qarlugs—eleven tribes in all, each with its own superintendent—and in battle the two subject tribes always led the van.

sentences.zh: 李林甫以楊慎矜屈附於己，九月，甲戌，復以慎矜為御史中丞，充諸道鑄錢使。

translations.literal: Li Linfu, because Yang Shenjing had bowed and attached himself to him, in the ninth month on the day jiaxu again appointed Shenjing Censor-in-Chief and additionally made him commissioner for casting coin in all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yang Shenjing had submitted to him, Li Linfu in the ninth month, on jiaxu day, restored him as censor-in-chief and also made him commissioner for casting coin in all circuits.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，癸巳，上幸驪山溫泉；

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the day guisi, the emperor visited Mount Li hot springs;
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on guisi day, the emperor went to the hot springs at Mount Li;

sentences.zh: 十一月，丁卯，還宮。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the day dingmao, he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on dingmao day, he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 術士蘇嘉慶上言：「遁甲術有九宮貴神，典司水旱，請立壇於東郊，祀以四孟月。」

translations.literal: Technician Su Jiaqing submitted, saying, "In the art of dunjia there are the Nine Palaces Noble Spirits, who preside over flood and drought. I request that an altar be established in the eastern suburbs and sacrifices be offered in the four first months of the seasons."
translations.idiomatic: Technician Su Jiaqing memorialized: "The dunjia art holds that the Nine Palaces Noble Spirits govern flood and drought. I ask that an altar be built in the eastern suburbs and sacrifices offered in the first month of each season."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 禮在昊天上帝下，太清宮、太廟上，所用牲玉，皆侔天地。

translations.literal: In ritual ranking it stood below the August Heaven God and above the Grand Purity Palace and the Imperial Ancestral Temple; the victims and jade used were all equal to those for Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Its rites ranked below August Heaven but above the Grand Purity Palace and the ancestral temple; the victims and jade offered matched those for Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 十二月，癸巳，置會昌縣於溫泉宮下。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day guisi, Huichang County was established below the Hot Spring Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on guisi day, Huichang County was established at the foot of the Hot Spring Palace.

sentences.zh: 戶部尚書裴寬素為上所重，李林甫恐其入相，忌之。

translations.literal: Minister of Revenue Pei Kuan had long been valued by the emperor; Li Linfu feared he might enter the chancellorship and was jealous of him.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of revenue Pei Kuan had long enjoyed the emperor's regard; Li Linfu, fearing he might become chancellor, envied him.

sentences.zh: 刑部尚書裴敦復擊海賊還，受請托，廣序軍功，寬微奏其事。

translations.literal: Minister of Justice Pei Dunfu, on returning from attacking sea bandits, had accepted entreaties and broadly set forth military achievements; Kuan subtly memorialized the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of justice Pei Dunfu, returning from campaigning against sea bandits, had taken bribes and inflated his battle honors; Pei Kuan quietly memorialized against him.

sentences.zh: 林甫以告敦復，敦復言寬亦嘗以親故屬敦復。

translations.literal: Linfu told Dunfu of this; Dunfu said that Kuan too had once asked favors of Dunfu on behalf of relatives and friends.
translations.idiomatic: Linfu informed Dunfu, who replied that Kuan too had once asked favors for his relatives and friends.

sentences.zh: 林甫曰：「君速奏之，勿後於人。」

translations.literal: Linfu said, "Memorialize swiftly—do not be later than others."
translations.idiomatic: Linfu said, "Memorialize at once—do not let anyone beat you to it."

sentences.zh: 敦復乃以五百金賂女官楊太真之姊，使言於上。

translations.literal: Dunfu then used five hundred in gold to bribe a sister of the female official Lady Yang Taizhen, having her speak to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Dunfu then bribed one of Lady Yang Taizhen's sisters with five hundred taels of gold to speak to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 甲午，寬坐貶睢陽太守。

translations.literal: On the day jiawu, Kuan was demoted on this charge to Prefect of Suiyang.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu day, Kuan was demoted to prefect of Suiyang.

sentences.zh: 初，武惠妃薨，上悼念不已，後宮數千，無當意者。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Consort Wu Huifei died, the emperor mourned her without cease; among the several thousand women of the inner palace, none suited his mind.
translations.idiomatic: After Consort Wu Huifei died, the emperor could not stop mourning her; among the thousands of women in the inner palace, none pleased him.

sentences.zh: 或言壽王妃楊氏之美，絕世無雙。

translations.literal: Someone spoke of the beauty of Princess of Shou Yang, saying she was without peer in the age.
translations.idiomatic: Someone spoke of the beauty of Lady Yang, consort of the Prince of Shou, saying she was without peer in the age.

sentences.zh: 上見而悅之，乃令妃自以其意乞為女官，號太真；

translations.literal: The emperor saw her and was pleased; he then had the consort herself, according to her own wish, beg to become a female official with the title Taizhen;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw her and was delighted; he had her petition, of her own accord, to become a female official titled Taizhen;

sentences.zh: 更為壽王娶左衛郎將韋昭訓女；

translations.literal: and arranged another marriage for the Prince of Shou, taking as his wife the daughter of Left Guard General Wei Zhaoxun;
translations.idiomatic: then found another bride for the Prince of Shou, marrying him to the daughter of Left Guard general Wei Zhaoxun;

sentences.zh: 潛內太真宮中。

translations.literal: and secretly brought Taizhen into the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: and secretly installed Taizhen in the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 太真肌態豐艷，曉音律，性警穎，善承迎上意，不期歲，寵遇如惠妃，宮中號曰「娘子」，凡儀體皆如皇后。

translations.literal: Taizhen's flesh and bearing were full and radiant; she understood music, was by nature sharp and clever, and was skilled at meeting the emperor's wishes. Before a year had passed, favor and treatment were like those of Consort Wu Huifei; within the palace she was called "My Lady," and in all ceremonial forms she was as an empress.
translations.idiomatic: Taizhen was voluptuous and radiant, understood music, and was quick-witted and skilled at pleasing the emperor. Within a year her favor matched that of Consort Wu Huifei; the palace called her "My Lady," and in ceremony she was treated like an empress.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，以宗女為和義公主，嫁寧遠奉化王阿悉爛達干。

translations.literal: On the day guimao, an imperial clanswoman was made Princess of Harmony and given in marriage to Ashilan Daghan, King of Ningyuan who had submitted to transformation.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao day, an imperial clanswoman was made Princess of Harmony and married to Ashilan Daghan, the submitting king of Ningyuan.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，上祀九宮貴神，赦天下。

translations.literal: On the day guichou, the emperor sacrificed to the Nine Palaces Noble Spirits and pardoned all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou day, the emperor sacrificed to the Nine Palaces Noble Spirits and issued a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 初令百姓十八為中，二十三成丁。

translations.literal: For the first time it was ordered that common people at eighteen were counted as middling and at twenty-three became adult males for service.
translations.idiomatic: For the first time the court ruled that commoners counted as middling age at eighteen and reached full adult service status at twenty-three.

sentences.zh: 初，上自東都還，李林甫知上厭巡幸，乃與牛仙客謀增近道粟賦及和糴以實關中。

translations.literal: Earlier, after the emperor returned from the Eastern Capital, Li Linfu knew the emperor was weary of touring, and therefore with Niu Xianke plotted to increase grain levies on the nearby routes and government purchases at fair price to fill Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor returned from the Eastern Capital, Li Linfu knew he had grown weary of touring and, with Niu Xianke, plotted to increase grain levies on nearby routes and government grain purchases to fill the stores of Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 數年，蓄積稍豐。

translations.literal: Within several years, stored accumulations grew somewhat abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years the granaries grew fairly full.

sentences.zh: 上從容謂高力士曰：「朕不出長安近十年，天下無事，朕欲高居無為，悉以政事委林甫，何如？」

translations.literal: The emperor said at ease to Gao Lishi, "I have not left Chang'an for nearly ten years; all under Heaven is without trouble. I wish to dwell on high in nonaction and entirely entrust government affairs to Linfu. What do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said casually to Gao Lishi, "I have scarcely left Chang'an in nearly ten years, and all under Heaven is at peace. I wish to retire into nonaction and entrust all government to Linfu. What do you think?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「天子巡狩，古之制也。

translations.literal: He replied, "The Son of Heaven's tours of inspection are an ancient institution.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "The Son of Heaven's tours of inspection are an ancient institution.

sentences.zh: 且天下大柄，不可假人；

translations.literal: Moreover, the great handles of all under Heaven may not be lent to another;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the great handles of power may not be lent to another;

sentences.zh: 彼威勢既成，誰敢復議之者！」

translations.literal: once his authority and power are formed, who will dare speak against him again!"
translations.idiomatic: once his authority is established, who will dare speak against him again!"

sentences.zh: 上不悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 力士頓首自陳：「臣狂疾，發妄言，罪當死！」

translations.literal: Lishi bowed his head to the ground and declared himself, saying, "Your subject suffers from mad illness and uttered reckless words; the crime deserves death!"
translations.idiomatic: Lishi kowtowed and said, "I spoke in madness; my crime deserves death!"

sentences.zh: 上乃為力士置酒，左右皆呼萬歲。

translations.literal: The emperor then set out wine for Lishi, and those at his side all cried "Ten thousand years!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then set out wine for Lishi, and those around them all cried "Long live the emperor!"

sentences.zh: 力士自是不敢深言天下事矣。

translations.literal: From then on Lishi himself did not dare speak deeply on affairs of all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Lishi no longer dared speak frankly about affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 玄宗至道大聖大明孝皇帝中之下天寶四年（

translations.literal: Middle-lower portion of the reign of Emperor Xuanzong, Sagacious Emperor of the Supreme Way, Great Brightness, and Filial Piety—Tianbao year 4 (
translations.idiomatic: Middle-lower portion of the reign of Emperor Xuanzong of the Tang—Tianbao year 4 (

sentences.zh: 乙酉，公元七四五年）

translations.literal: yiyou, corresponding to the year 745 CE)
translations.idiomatic: yiyou, AD 745)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，庚午，上謂宰相曰：「朕比以甲子日，於宮中為壇，為百姓祈福，朕自草黃素置案上，俄飛升天，聞空中語去：『聖壽延長。』

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the day gengwu, the emperor said to the chancellors, "Recently on a jiazi day I set up an altar in the palace to pray for blessings for the common people. I myself drafted a yellow silk text and placed it on the table; presently it flew up into Heaven. I heard a voice in the air depart, saying, 'May the sage's years be prolonged.'
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on gengwu day, the emperor told the chancellors, "Recently on a jiazi day I set up an altar in the palace to pray for the people. I wrote a prayer on yellow silk and placed it on the table; it suddenly flew up into the sky, and I heard a voice from the air say, 'May the sage's years be prolonged.'

sentences.zh: 又朕於嵩山煉藥成，亦置壇上，及夜，左右欲收之，又聞空中語云：『藥未須收，此自守護。』

translations.literal: Again, when I had finished refining medicine on Mount Song, I also placed it on the altar; when night came and those at my side wished to gather it in, again I heard a voice in the air say, 'The medicine need not yet be gathered; this will guard itself.'
translations.idiomatic: Again, when I had finished refining elixirs on Mount Song, I placed them on the altar; that night, when my attendants tried to collect them, I again heard a voice from the air say, 'The elixir need not be gathered yet; it will guard itself.'

sentences.zh: 達曙乃收之。」

translations.literal: Only at dawn was it gathered in."
translations.idiomatic: Only at dawn did they collect it."

sentences.zh: 太子、諸王、宰相，皆上表賀。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince, the princes, and the chancellors all submitted congratulatory memorials.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince, the princes, and the chancellors all submitted congratulatory memorials.

sentences.zh: 回紇懷仁可汗擊突厥白眉可汗，殺之，傳首京師。

translations.literal: The Uyghur Huairan Khagan attacked the Türk White-Eyebrow Khagan, killed him, and sent his head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghur khagan Huairan attacked the Türk White-Eyebrow Khagan, killed him, and sent his head to the capital.

sentences.zh: 突厥毘伽可敦帥眾來降。

translations.literal: The Türk Pijia Khatun led her people to submit.
translations.idiomatic: The Türk khatun Pijia led her people in surrender.

sentences.zh: 於是北邊晏然，烽燧無警矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon the northern frontier was tranquil, and beacon fires were without alarm.
translations.idiomatic: The northern frontier was now tranquil, and the beacon towers stood without alarm.

sentences.zh: 回紇斥地愈廣，東際室韋，西抵金山，南跨大漠，盡有突厥故地。

translations.literal: The Uyghurs extended their territory ever wider: east to the Shiwei, west to Mount Jin, south across the Great Desert, possessing all the old Türk lands.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghurs extended their territory ever wider: east to the Shiwei, west to Mount Jin, south across the Great Desert, holding all the old Türk lands.

sentences.zh: 懷仁卒，子磨延啜立，號葛勒可汗。

translations.literal: Huairan died; his son Moyanchuo succeeded and took the title Gele Khagan.
translations.idiomatic: When Huairan died, his son Moyanchuo succeeded him as khagan Gele.

sentences.zh: 二月，己酉，以朔方節度使王忠嗣兼河東節度使。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the day jiyou, Shuofang Military Commissioner Wang Zhongsi was additionally made military commissioner of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on jiyou day, Shuofang commissioner Wang Zhongsi was also made commissioner of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 忠嗣少以勇敢自負，及鎮方面，專以持重安邊為務，常曰：「太平之將，但當撫循訓練士卒而已，不可疲中國之力以邀功名。」

translations.literal: Zhongsi in youth prided himself on bravery; when he governed a frontier command, he devoted himself solely to steadiness in pacifying the border and often said, "A general in times of peace should only comfort, guide, and train the soldiers; he must not exhaust the strength of China to seek fame and merit."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongsi had once prided himself on bravery, but once he governed the frontier he devoted himself to steady border defense and often said, "A general in peacetime should only comfort and train his troops; he must not exhaust the empire's strength to win glory."

sentences.zh: 有漆弓百五十斤，常貯之橐中，以示不用。

translations.literal: He had a lacquered bow of a hundred fifty jin and regularly kept it stored in his bag to show that he did not use it.
translations.idiomatic: He kept a lacquered bow weighing a hundred fifty jin in his bag to show that he did not use it.

sentences.zh: 軍中日夜思戰，忠嗣多遣謀人伺其間隙，見可勝，然後興師，故出必有功。

translations.literal: Day and night in the army they longed for battle; Zhongsi often sent spies to watch for openings, and only when victory was possible would he raise the army—therefore whenever he went out he was sure to achieve merit.
translations.idiomatic: His troops were eager for battle day and night, but Zhongsi sent spies to watch for openings and marched only when victory was assured; every campaign he undertook succeeded.

sentences.zh: 既兼兩道節制，自朔方至去雲中，邊陲數千里，要害之地，悉列置城堡，斥地各數百里。

translations.literal: Once he held command of both circuits, from Shuofang to Yunzhong along several thousand li of the frontier, at every strategic place he fully arrayed and set up fortresses and castles, extending his territory several hundred li in each direction.
translations.idiomatic: Once he commanded both circuits, from Shuofang to Yunzhong he fortified every strategic point along thousands of li of frontier, extending his sway for hundreds of li in every direction.

sentences.zh: 邊人以為自張仁但之後，將帥皆不及。

translations.literal: Border peoples considered that since Zhang Rendan, no general had matched him.
translations.idiomatic: On the frontier he was held to be unmatched among commanders since Zhang Rendan.

sentences.zh: 三月，壬申，上以外孫獨孤氏為靜樂公主，嫁契丹王李懷節；

translations.literal: In the third month, on the day renshen, the emperor made his maternal granddaughter of the Dugu clan Princess of Jingle and gave her in marriage to the Khitan king Li Huaijie;
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on renshen day, the emperor made his Dugu granddaughter Princess of Jingle and married her to the Khitan king Li Huaijie;

sentences.zh: 甥楊氏為宜芳公主，嫁奚王李延寵。

translations.literal: his nephew's daughter of the Yang clan was made Princess of Yifang and given in marriage to the Xi king Li Yanchong.
translations.idiomatic: and his Yang clanswoman niece was made Princess of Yifang and married to the Xi king Li Yanchong.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，以刑部尚書裴敦復充嶺南五府經略等使。

translations.literal: On the day yisi, Minister of Justice Pei Dunfu was appointed to serve as commissioner for the five prefectures of Lingnan and related posts.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi day, Minister of Justice Pei Dunfu was appointed commissioner for the five Lingnan prefectures.

sentences.zh: 五月，壬申，敦復坐逗留不之官，貶淄川太守，以光祿少卿彭杲代之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the day renshen, Dunfu was charged with lingering and not proceeding to his post; he was demoted to Prefect of Zichuan, and Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments Peng Gao replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on renshen day, Dunfu was charged with delaying his departure and demoted to prefect of Zichuan; Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments Peng Gao replaced him.

sentences.zh: 上嘉敦復平海賊之功，故李林甫陷之。

translations.literal: The emperor had praised Dunfu's achievement in pacifying the sea bandits; therefore Li Linfu framed him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had praised Dunfu for defeating the sea bandits, and Li Linfu engineered his fall.

sentences.zh: 李適之與李林甫爭權有隙。

translations.literal: Li Shizhi and Li Linfu contended for power and had a rift between them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shizhi and Li Linfu were rivals for power and deeply at odds.

sentences.zh: 適之領兵部尚書，附馬張□為侍郎，林甫亦惡之，使人發兵部銓曹奸利事，收吏六十餘人付京兆與御史對鞫之，數日，竟不得其情。

translations.literal: Shizhi held the post of Minister of War, and Imperial Son-in-Law Zhang Ya served as vice minister; Linfu also hated them and had men expose corrupt profit-seeking in the War Ministry's selection office, seizing more than sixty clerks and handing them to the Metropolitan Prefecture and the Censorate for joint interrogation; after several days they still could not obtain the facts.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhi was minister of war, and Imperial Son-in-Law Zhang Ya was his vice minister; Linfu hated them too and exposed corruption in the War Ministry selection office, arresting more than sixty clerks for interrogation by the metropolitan prefecture and the censorate—but after several days no proof emerged.

sentences.zh: 京兆尹蕭炅使法曹吉溫鞫之。

translations.literal: Metropolitan Prefect Xiao Jiong had Legal Officer Ji Wen interrogate them.
translations.idiomatic: Metropolitan Prefect Xiao Jiong put Legal Officer Ji Wen in charge of the interrogation.

sentences.zh: 溫入院，置兵部吏於外，先於後廳取二重囚訊之，或杖或壓，號呼之聲，所不忍聞；

translations.literal: Wen entered the courtyard, placed the War Ministry clerks outside, and first in the rear hall took two serious criminals for questioning, beating or crushing them; the sound of their cries was unbearable to hear;
translations.idiomatic: Wen entered the compound, left the War Ministry clerks outside, and in the rear hall first tortured two hardened criminals—beating and crushing them until their cries were unbearable;

sentences.zh: 皆曰：「苟存餘生，乞紙盡答。」

translations.literal: both saying, "If we may preserve a remnant of life, we beg paper to answer everything."
translations.idiomatic: both begging, "Spare our lives and we will confess everything in writing."

sentences.zh: 兵部吏素聞溫之慘酷，引入，皆自誣服，無敢違溫意者。

translations.literal: The War Ministry clerks had long heard of Wen's cruelty; when brought in, all falsely confessed of themselves, and none dared go against Wen's intent.
translations.idiomatic: The War Ministry clerks, who knew Wen's cruelty, were brought in and all falsely confessed; none dared defy him.

sentences.zh: 頃刻而獄成，驗囚無榜掠之跡。

translations.literal: In an instant the case was complete; when the prisoners were examined there were no marks of beating.
translations.idiomatic: The case was closed in moments, and examination of the prisoners showed no marks of beating.

sentences.zh: 六月，辛亥，敕誚責前後知銓侍郎及判南曹郎官而宥之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day xinhai, an edict rebuked the former and current vice ministers in charge of selection and the officials who judged the Southern Office, yet pardoned them.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on xinhai day, an edict rebuked the past and present selection vice ministers and Southern Office judges but pardoned them.

sentences.zh: □，均之兄；

translations.literal: Ya was Jun's brother;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ya was Zhang Jun's brother;

sentences.zh: 溫，頊之弟子也。

translations.literal: Wen was a disciple of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Wen was a disciple of Xu Hao.

sentences.zh: 溫始為新豐丞，太子文學薛嶷存溫才，上召見，顧嶷曰：「是一不良人，朕不用也。」

translations.literal: Wen had first been magistrate of Xinfeng; Palace Literary Companion Xue Yi recommended Wen's talent, and the emperor summoned him for an audience. Turning to Yi he said, "This is an ill-natured man; I will not employ him."
translations.idiomatic: Wen had begun as magistrate of Xinfeng; Palace literary companion Xue Yi recommended his talent, and when the emperor summoned him he told Yi, "This is a bad man; I will not use him."

sentences.zh: 蕭炅為河南尹，嘗坐事，西台遣溫往按之，溫治炅甚急。

translations.literal: Xiao Jiong was Henan Prefect; he once ran afoul of the law, and the Western Bureau sent Wen to investigate him; Wen prosecuted Jiong very harshly.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Jiong was Henan prefect he once ran afoul of the law; the censorate sent Wen to investigate, and Wen prosecuted him harshly.

sentences.zh: 及溫為萬年丞，未幾，炅為京兆尹。

translations.literal: When Wen became assistant magistrate of Wannian, before long Jiong became Metropolitan Prefect.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen became assistant magistrate of Wannian, Jiong soon became metropolitan prefect.

sentences.zh: 溫素與高力士相結，力士自禁中歸，溫度炅必往謝官，乃先詣力士，與之談謔，握手甚歡。

translations.literal: Wen had long been allied with Gao Lishi; when Lishi returned from within the palace, Wen reckoned that Jiong would surely come to thank him for his appointment, and therefore went first to Lishi, talking and jesting with him and clasping hands in great cordiality.
translations.idiomatic: Wen was allied with Gao Lishi; when Lishi returned from the palace, Wen guessed Jiong would come to thank him for his appointment and went first to Lishi, chatting and laughing with him in warm familiarity.

sentences.zh: 炅後至，溫陽為驚避。

translations.literal: Jiong arrived afterward; Wen pretended to start in alarm and withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiong arrived, Wen feigned surprise and drew back.

sentences.zh: 力士呼曰：「吉七不須避。」

translations.literal: Lishi called out, "Ji the Seventh need not withdraw."
translations.idiomatic: Lishi called out, "Ji the Seventh need not withdraw."

sentences.zh: 謂炅曰：「此亦吾故人也。」

translations.literal: He said to Jiong, "This too is an old friend of mine."
translations.idiomatic: He told Jiong, "He is an old friend of mine as well."

sentences.zh: 召還，與炅坐。

translations.literal: He summoned Wen back and had him sit with Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: He called Wen back and had him sit with Jiong.

sentences.zh: 炅接之甚恭，不敢以前事為怨。

translations.literal: Jiong received him very respectfully and did not dare hold the earlier affair as a grudge.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong received him with great respect and dared not bear a grudge over the past.

sentences.zh: 他日，溫謁炅曰：「曩者溫不敢隳國家法，自今請洗心事公。」

translations.literal: Another day Wen called on Jiong and said, "Formerly Wen did not dare destroy the laws of the state; from now on I beg to cleanse my heart and serve you."
translations.idiomatic: Another day Wen visited Jiong and said, "Before I would not break the law; from now on I ask to serve you with a clean heart."

sentences.zh: 炅遂與盡歡，引為法曹。

translations.literal: Jiong then drank with him to the full and brought him in as Legal Officer.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong drank with him freely and appointed him legal officer.

sentences.zh: 及林甫欲除不附己者，求治獄吏，炅薦溫於林甫；

translations.literal: When Linfu wished to remove those who did not attach themselves to him, he sought officers skilled in handling cases; Jiong recommended Wen to Linfu;
translations.idiomatic: When Linfu sought to destroy opponents, he looked for skilled interrogators; Jiong recommended Wen to him;

sentences.zh: 林甫得之，大喜。

translations.literal: Linfu obtained him and was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Linfu was delighted to have him.

sentences.zh: 溫常曰：「若遇知己，南山白額虎不足縛也。」

translations.literal: Wen often said, "If one meets a true patron, even the white-browed tiger of the southern mountains is not enough to bind one."
translations.idiomatic: Wen often said, "With the right patron, even the white-browed tiger of the southern mountains is nothing."

sentences.zh: 時又有杭州人羅希奭，為吏深刻，林甫引之，自御史台主簿再遷殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: At the time there was also Luo Xiyi of Hangzhou, harsh and penetrating as an officer; Linfu brought him in, and from chief clerk of the Censorate he was promoted again to Attending Censor Within the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Luo Xiyi of Hangzhou, a ruthless officer whom Linfu promoted from chief clerk of the censorate to palace attending censor.

sentences.zh: 二人皆隨林甫所欲深淺，鍛煉成獄，無能自脫者，時人謂之「羅鉗吉網」。

translations.literal: Both men, according to the depth or shallowness of Linfu's wishes, forged and refined cases to completion; none could extricate themselves, and people of the time called them "Luo's pincers and Ji's net."
translations.idiomatic: Both men forged cases to Linfu's liking; none could escape them, and people called them "Luo's pincers and Ji's net."

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，壬午，冊韋昭訓女為壽王妃。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the day renwu, the daughter of Wei Zhaoxun was invested as consort of the Prince of Shou.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on renwu day, the daughter of Wei Zhaoxun was invested as consort of the Prince of Shou.

sentences.zh: 八月，壬寅，冊楊太真為貴妃；

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the day renyin, Lady Yang Taizhen was invested as Noble Consort;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on renyin day, Lady Yang Taizhen was invested as Noble Consort;

sentences.zh: 贈其父玄琰兵部尚書，以其叔父玄珪為光祿卿，從兄銛為殿中少監，金奇為駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: her father Xuanyan was posthumously given the post of Minister of War; her uncle Xuangui was made Director of the Court for the Imperial Clan; her cousin Xian was made Vice Director of the Palace Service; and Jin Qi was made Commandant of the Imperial Sons-in-Law.
translations.idiomatic: her father Xuanyan was posthumously made minister of war; her uncle Xuangui was made director of the court for the imperial clan; her cousin Xian was made vice director of the palace service; and Jin Qi was made commandant of the imperial sons-in-law.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，冊武惠妃女為太華公主，命金奇尚之。

translations.literal: On the day guimao, the daughter of Consort Wu Huifei was invested as Princess of Taihua, and Jin Qi was ordered to marry her.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao day, the daughter of Consort Wu Huifei was made Princess of Taihua and given to Jin Qi in marriage.

sentences.zh: 及貴妃三姊，皆賜第京師，寵貴赫然。

translations.literal: Together with the Noble Consort's three elder sisters, all were granted mansions in the capital, and favor and eminence blazed forth.
translations.idiomatic: The Noble Consort's three elder sisters were also given mansions in the capital, and their splendor was unmistakable.

sentences.zh: 楊釗，貴妃之從祖兄也，不學無行，為宗黨所鄙。

translations.literal: Yang Zhao was a cousin of the Noble Consort's grandfather's generation; he did not study and had no proper conduct, and was despised by the clan.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhao, a cousin of the Noble Consort's grandfather's generation, was uneducated and dissolute and despised by his clan.

sentences.zh: 從軍於蜀，得新都尉；

translations.literal: He followed the army in Shu and obtained the post of Wei of Xindu;
translations.idiomatic: He joined the army in Shu and became magistrate of Xindu;

sentences.zh: 考滿，家貧不能自歸，新政富民鮮于仲通常資給之。

translations.literal: when his term of evaluation ended, his family was poor and he could not return home on his own; Xianyu Zhongtong, a wealthy man of Xinzheng, regularly supplied him with funds.
translations.idiomatic: when his term ended he was too poor to return home, and Xianyu Zhongtong, a wealthy man of Xinzheng, regularly supported him.

sentences.zh: 楊玄琰卒於蜀，釗往來其家，遂與其中女通。

translations.literal: Yang Xuanyan died in Shu; Zhao went back and forth to his household and thereupon had relations with one of the daughters within.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Xuanyan died in Shu, Zhao frequented the household and took up with one of the daughters.

sentences.zh: 鮮于仲通名向，以字行，頗讀書，有材智，劍南節度使章仇兼瓊引為採訪支使，委以心腹。

translations.literal: Xianyu Zhongtong's given name was Xiang; he was known by his style name, read books considerably, and had talent and wisdom. Jiannan Military Commissioner Zhang Qiu Jianqiong brought him in as investigation support officer and entrusted him as a confidant.
