translations.idiomatic: Xianyu Zhongtong, whose given name was Xiang, was known by his style name; he was well read and capable. Jiannan commissioner Zhang Qiu Jianqiong made him investigation support officer and treated him as a confidant.

sentences.zh: 嘗從容謂仲通曰：「今吾獨為上所厚，苟無內援，必為李林甫所危。

translations.literal: He once said at ease to Zhongtong, "Now I alone am deeply favored by the emperor; if I have no support within the palace, I shall surely be endangered by Li Linfu.
translations.idiomatic: He once told Zhongtong frankly, "I alone enjoy the emperor's deep favor now; without support inside the palace I shall surely be ruined by Li Linfu.

sentences.zh: 聞楊妃新得幸，人未敢附之。

translations.literal: I hear that Consort Yang has newly won favor, and people do not yet dare attach themselves to her.
translations.idiomatic: I hear Consort Yang has newly won favor, and no one yet dares court her.

sentences.zh: 子能為我至長安與其家相結，吾無患矣。」

translations.literal: Can you go to Chang'an for me and form ties with her family? Then I shall have no worry."
translations.idiomatic: Can you go to Chang'an for me and win over her family? Then I shall be safe."

sentences.zh: 仲通曰：「仲通蜀人，未嘗游上國，恐敗公事。

translations.literal: Zhongtong said, "Zhongtong is a man of Shu and has never traveled in the upper realm; I fear I may ruin the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongtong replied, "I am a man of Shu and have never been to the capital; I fear I may ruin your plan.

sentences.zh: 今為公更求得一人。」

translations.literal: I will now find another man for you."
translations.idiomatic: Let me find someone else for you."

sentences.zh: 因言釗本末。

translations.literal: Thereupon he related Zhao's background from beginning to end.
translations.idiomatic: He then told Zhao's whole story.

sentences.zh: 兼瓊引見釗，儀觀甚偉，言辭敏給；

translations.literal: Jianqiong had Zhao presented; his bearing and appearance were very imposing and his speech quick and ready;
translations.idiomatic: Jianqiong received Zhao, who was imposing in appearance and quick of speech;

sentences.zh: 兼瓊大喜，即闢為推官，往來浸親密。

translations.literal: Jianqiong was greatly pleased and at once appointed him investigating officer; their coming and going grew ever more intimate.
translations.idiomatic: Jianqiong was delighted and at once made him investigating officer; they grew increasingly close.

sentences.zh: 乃使之獻春彩於京師，將別，謂曰：「有少物在郫，以具一日之糧，子過，可取之。」

translations.literal: He then had him present spring silks in the capital. As they were about to part he said, "There are a few things in Pi to supply one day's provisions; when you pass by, you may take them."
translations.idiomatic: He sent him to present spring silks in the capital. As Zhao was leaving he said, "I have a few things in Pi for one day's provisions—stop and take them on your way."

sentences.zh: 釗至郫，兼瓊使親信大繼蜀貨精美者遺之，可直萬緡。

translations.literal: When Zhao reached Pi, Jianqiong had a trusted agent Da Ji present him with the finest goods of Shu, worth ten thousand strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao reached Pi, Jianqiong's agent Da Ji gave him the finest Shu goods, worth ten thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 釗大喜過望，晝夜兼行，至長安，歷抵諸妹，以蜀貨遺之，曰：「此章仇公所贈也。」

translations.literal: Zhao was delighted beyond expectation, traveled day and night without pause, reached Chang'an, and called on each of the sisters in turn, presenting them with Shu goods and saying, "These were given by Lord Zhang Qiu."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao was overjoyed and hurried day and night to Chang'an, visiting each sister and giving them Shu goods, saying, "These are gifts from Lord Zhang Qiu."

sentences.zh: 時中女新寡，釗遂館於其室，中分蜀貨以與之。

translations.literal: At the time the middle sister was newly widowed; Zhao thereupon lodged in her house and shared the Shu goods with her.
translations.idiomatic: The middle sister was newly widowed; Zhao lodged with her and shared the goods with her.

sentences.zh: 於是諸楊日夜譽兼瓊；

translations.literal: Thereupon the various Yangs day and night praised Jianqiong;
translations.idiomatic: The Yang clan then praised Jianqiong day and night;

sentences.zh: 且言釗善樗蒲，引之見上，得隨供奉官出入禁中，改金吾兵曹參軍。

translations.literal: and added that Zhao was skilled at chuck-a-luck, had him introduced to the emperor, obtained permission to enter and leave the forbidden precincts as an attendant officer, and was changed to military staff officer of the Golden Guard.
translations.idiomatic: and said Zhao was skilled at dice; he was introduced to the emperor, allowed to enter the inner palace as an attendant officer, and made military staff officer of the Golden Guard.

sentences.zh: 九月，癸未，以陝郡太守、江淮租庸轉運使韋堅為刑部尚書，罷其諸使，以御使中丞楊慎矜代之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the day guiwei, Wei Jian, Prefect of Shan Commandery and commissioner for Jiang-Huai rent, corvée, and transport, was made Minister of Justice; his various commissions were abolished, and Censor-in-Chief Yang Shenjing replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on guiwei day, Wei Jian, prefect of Shan and Jiang-Huai transport commissioner, was made minister of justice; his commissions were abolished and Censor-in-Chief Yang Shenjing replaced him.

sentences.zh: 堅妻姜氏，皎之女，林甫之舅子也，故林甫暱之。

translations.literal: Jian's wife was of the Jiang clan, a daughter of Jiang, and a nephew by marriage of Linfu; therefore Linfu was close to him.
translations.idiomatic: Jian's wife was Jiang's daughter and Linfu's nephew by marriage, so Linfu had been fond of him.

sentences.zh: 及堅以通漕有寵於上，遂有入相之志，又與李適之善；

translations.literal: When Jian, because of opening the canal transport, won favor with the emperor, he then had the ambition to enter the chancellorship, and was also on good terms with Li Shizhi;
translations.idiomatic: But when Jian won favor for opening canal transport, he aspired to the chancellorship and befriended Li Shizhi;

sentences.zh: 林甫由是惡之，故遷以美宮，實奪之權也。

translations.literal: Linfu therefore hated him and so transferred him to a fine palace appointment, in reality stripping him of power.
translations.idiomatic: Linfu therefore hated him and gave him a handsome court post that in fact stripped him of power.

sentences.zh: 安祿山欲以邊功市寵，數侵掠奚、契丹；

translations.literal: An Lushan wished to purchase favor with frontier achievements and repeatedly raided the Xi and Khitan;
translations.idiomatic: An Lushan sought favor through frontier victories and repeatedly raided the Xi and Khitan;

sentences.zh: 奚、契丹各殺公主以叛，祿山討破之。

translations.literal: the Xi and Khitan each killed their princesses and rebelled; Lushan campaigned and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: each people killed their Tang princesses and rebelled; Lushan defeated them.

sentences.zh: 隴右節度使皇甫惟明與吐蕃戰於石堡城，為虜所敗，副將褚□戰死。

translations.literal: Longyou Military Commissioner Huangfu Weiming fought Tibet at Shibao City, was defeated by the enemy, and Vice General Chu Sizhuang died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Longyou commissioner Huangfu Weiming fought Tibet at Shibao City, was defeated, and Vice General Chu Sizhuang was killed.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，甲午，安祿山奏：「臣討契丹至北平郡，夢先朝名將李靖、李勣從臣求食。」

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the day jiawu, An Lushan memorialized, "Your subject, campaigning against the Khitan as far as Beiping Commandery, dreamed that famed generals of the former dynasty, Li Jing and Li Ji, followed your subject begging for food."
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on jiawu day, An Lushan memorialized: "While campaigning against the Khitan as far as Beiping Commandery, I dreamed that the famed generals Li Jing and Li Ji followed me begging for food."

sentences.zh: 遂命立廟。

translations.literal: He thereupon ordered a temple established.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered a temple built.

sentences.zh: 又奏薦奠之日，廟梁產芝。

translations.literal: He also memorialized that on the day of offering sacrifices, fungus sprang forth on the temple beams.
translations.idiomatic: He also reported that on the day of the sacrifice, auspicious fungus appeared on the temple beams.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，上幸驪山溫泉。

translations.literal: On the day dingyou, the emperor visited Mount Li hot springs.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou day the emperor went to the hot springs at Mount Li.

sentences.zh: 上以戶部郎中王□為戶口色役使，敕賜百姓復除。

translations.literal: The emperor appointed Ministry of Revenue Section Chief Wang Yue as commissioner for household registers and corvée labor, and issued an edict granting the common people exemptions.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed Ministry of Revenue section chief Wang Yue commissioner for household registers and corvée labor and issued an edict granting tax exemptions to the people.

sentences.zh: □奏征其輦運之費，廣張錢數，又使市本郡輕貨，百姓所輸乃甚於不復除。

translations.literal: Yue memorialized to levy the cost of cart transport, greatly inflated the sums of money, and also had people purchase light goods of their home commanderies; what the common people paid in was even greater than if there had been no exemption.
translations.idiomatic: Yue levied transport fees, inflated the amounts, and forced people to buy light goods from their home commanderies; what the people paid exceeded what they would have owed without the exemption.

sentences.zh: 舊制，戍邊者免其租庸，六歲而更。

translations.literal: By old regulation, those garrisoning the frontier were exempted from rent and corvée, and were rotated every six years.
translations.idiomatic: By old regulation, frontier garrison troops were exempt from rent and corvée and rotated every six years.

sentences.zh: 時邊將恥敗，士卒死者皆不申牒，貫籍不除。

translations.literal: At the time frontier generals were ashamed of defeat; soldiers who died were not reported in memorials, and their names were not struck from the registers.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier generals, ashamed of defeat, did not report dead soldiers, and their names remained on the registers.

sentences.zh: 王□志在聚斂，以有籍無人者皆為避課，按籍戍邊六歲之外，悉征其租庸，有並征三十年者，民無所訴。

translations.literal: Wang Yue's aim was to amass wealth; he treated all who had registers but no persons as evading tax, and according to the registers, beyond six years of frontier garrison service, he collected all their rent and corvée; some were taxed for as many as thirty years together, and the people had nowhere to appeal.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yue sought to amass wealth; he treated every name on the registers with no living holder as tax evasion and collected rent and corvée for up to thirty years beyond the six-year rotation, and the people had no recourse.

sentences.zh: 上在位久，用度日侈，後宮賞賜無節，不欲數於左、右藏取之。

translations.literal: The emperor had been on the throne a long time; expenditures grew daily more extravagant, and rewards in the inner palace were without limit; he did not wish frequently to take from the Left and Right Treasuries.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had reigned long; court spending grew lavish and inner-palace gifts boundless, and he did not wish to draw often on the state treasuries.

sentences.zh: □探知上指，歲貢額外錢帛百億萬，貯於內庫，以供宮中宴賜，曰：「此皆不出於租庸調，無預經費。」

translations.literal: Yue probed the emperor's intent and each year presented extra money and silk amounting to ten billion, storing it in the inner treasury to supply palace feasts and gifts, saying, "These all do not come from rent, corvée, and the equalization tax; they do not touch regular expenditures."
translations.idiomatic: Yue sensed the emperor's wishes and each year presented extra revenues of a hundred million strings, stored in the inner treasury for palace feasts and gifts, claiming, "These do not come from rent, corvée, or the equalization tax and do not touch regular expenditures."

sentences.zh: 上以□為能富國，益厚遇之。

translations.literal: The emperor considered Yue able to enrich the state and treated him still more generously.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thought Yue could enrich the state and treated him still more generously.

sentences.zh: □務為割剝以求媚，中外嗟怨。

translations.literal: Yue strove to extort and strip in order to seek favor; within and without the court there were sighs of resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Yue extorted the people to win favor, and resentment spread through the court and the realm.

sentences.zh: 丙子，以□為御史中丞、京畿採訪使。

translations.literal: On the day bingzi, Yue was made Censor-in-Chief and investigation commissioner for the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi day, Yue was made censor-in-chief and investigation commissioner for the capital region.

sentences.zh: 楊釗侍宴禁中，專掌樗蒲文簿，鉤校精密。

translations.literal: Yang Zhao attended banquets within the forbidden precincts, exclusively managing chuck-a-luck account books with meticulous auditing.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhao attended palace banquets, keeping the dice accounts with meticulous precision.

sentences.zh: 上賞其強明，曰：「好度支郎。」

translations.literal: The emperor praised his forceful clarity and said, "A fine revenue officer."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his sharp competence and said, "A fine revenue officer."

sentences.zh: 諸楊數征此言於上，又以屬王□，□因奏充判官。

translations.literal: The various Yangs repeatedly cited this saying to the emperor, and also entrusted Zhao to Wang Yue; Yue thereupon memorialized to appoint him as his assistant judge.
translations.idiomatic: The Yang clan repeated this remark to the emperor and recommended Zhao to Wang Yue, who memorialized to make him his assistant judge.

sentences.zh: 十二月，戊戌，上還宮。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day wuxu, the emperor returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on wuxu day, the emperor returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 玄宗至道大聖大明孝皇帝中之下天寶五年（

translations.literal: Middle-lower portion of the reign of Emperor Xuanzong, Sagacious Emperor of the Supreme Way, Great Brightness, and Filial Piety—Tianbao year 5 (
translations.idiomatic: Middle-lower portion of the reign of Emperor Xuanzong of the Tang—Tianbao year 5 (

sentences.zh: 丙戌，公元七四六年）

translations.literal: bingxu, corresponding to the year 746 CE)
translations.idiomatic: bingxu, AD 746)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，乙丑，以隴右節度使皇甫惟明兼河西節度使。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the day yichou, Longyou Military Commissioner Huangfu Weiming was additionally made military commissioner of Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on yichou day, Longyou commissioner Huangfu Weiming was also made commissioner of Hexi.

sentences.zh: 李適之性疏率，李林甫嘗謂適之曰：「華山有金礦，采之可以富國，主上未之知也。」

translations.literal: Li Shizhi was by nature careless and direct; Li Linfu once said to Shizhi, "Mount Hua has gold mines; mining them can enrich the state, and His Majesty does not yet know of this."
translations.idiomatic: Li Shizhi was frank and unguarded; Li Linfu once told him, "Mount Hua has gold mines that could enrich the state, and His Majesty does not yet know."

sentences.zh: 他日，適之因奏事言之。

translations.literal: Another day Shizhi, while memorializing on affairs, spoke of it.
translations.idiomatic: Another day Shizhi mentioned it while memorializing on other business.

sentences.zh: 上以問林甫，對曰：「臣久知之，但華山陛下本命，王氣所在，鑿之非宜，故不敢言。」

translations.literal: The emperor asked Linfu; he replied, "Your subject has long known of it, but Mount Hua is Your Majesty's natal place, where the royal qi resides; to dig there would not be fitting, and therefore your subject did not dare speak."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Linfu, who replied, "I have long known, but Mount Hua is Your Majesty's natal mountain, the seat of the royal qi; mining there would be inauspicious, so I dared not speak."

sentences.zh: 上以林甫為愛己，薄適之慮事不熟，謂曰：「自今奏事，宜先與林甫議之，無得輕脫。」

translations.literal: The emperor considered Linfu to love him and looked lightly on Shizhi for not having thought the matter through; he said, "From now on when you memorialize on affairs, you should first discuss them with Linfu; you must not speak rashly."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thought Linfu cared for him and blamed Shizhi for ill-considered counsel, saying, "From now on discuss all memorials with Linfu first; do not speak rashly."

sentences.zh: 適之由是束手矣。

translations.literal: Shizhi was thereby left with bound hands.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhi was effectively silenced.

sentences.zh: 適之既失恩，韋堅失權，益相親密，林甫愈惡之。

translations.literal: Shizhi having lost favor and Wei Jian having lost power, they became still more intimate with each other, and Linfu hated them all the more.
translations.idiomatic: With Shizhi out of favor and Wei Jian stripped of power, they drew closer together, and Linfu hated them all the more.

sentences.zh: 初，太子之立，非林甫意。

translations.literal: Earlier, the establishment of the Crown Prince had not been to Linfu's liking.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince's installation had not been Linfu's wish.

sentences.zh: 林甫恐異日為己禍，常有動搖東宮之志；

translations.literal: Linfu feared that in another day he would become a calamity to himself and often had the intent to shake the Eastern Palace;
translations.idiomatic: Linfu feared he would become a threat to him one day and often sought to undermine the Eastern Palace;

sentences.zh: 而堅，又太子之妃兄也。

translations.literal: while Jian was moreover the elder brother of the Crown Prince's consort.
translations.idiomatic: while Jian was the elder brother of the crown prince's consort.

sentences.zh: 皇甫惟明嘗為忠王友，時破吐蕃，入獻捷，見林甫專權，意頗不平。

translations.literal: Huangfu Weiming had once been friend to Prince Zhong; at the time he defeated Tibet and entered to present victory, he saw Linfu's monopoly of power and in his mind was rather discontent.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Weiming had once been tutor to Prince Zhong; after defeating Tibet and presenting his victory, he saw Linfu's monopoly of power and was deeply discontent.

sentences.zh: 時因見上，乘間微勸上去林甫。

translations.literal: At the time, on seeing the emperor, he seized an opening and subtly urged him to remove Linfu.
translations.idiomatic: On seeing the emperor he took the chance to urge him subtly to remove Linfu.

sentences.zh: 林甫知之，使楊慎矜密伺其所為。

translations.literal: Linfu learned of it and had Yang Shenjing secretly watch his actions.
translations.idiomatic: Linfu learned of this and had Yang Shenjing spy on them.

sentences.zh: 會正月望夜，太子出遊，與堅相見，堅又與惟明會於景龍觀道士之室。

translations.literal: It happened that on the night of the full moon in the first month the Crown Prince went out on an excursion and met with Jian; Jian also met with Weiming in the chamber of a Daoist priest at Jinglong Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of the first-month full moon the crown prince went out and met Jian; Jian also met Weiming in a Daoist priest's chamber at Jinglong Abbey.

sentences.zh: 慎矜發其事，以為堅戚裡，不應與邊將狎暱。

translations.literal: Shenjing exposed the affair, holding that Jian was a relative by marriage and ought not to be on intimate terms with frontier generals.
translations.idiomatic: Shenjing reported the affair, arguing that Jian, as a royal connection by marriage, should not be on familiar terms with frontier generals.

sentences.zh: 林甫因譖堅與惟明結謀，欲共立太子。

translations.literal: Linfu thereupon slandered Jian and Weiming as having formed a plot together to install the Crown Prince jointly.
translations.idiomatic: Linfu then accused Jian and Weiming of plotting together to put the crown prince on the throne.

sentences.zh: 堅、惟明下獄，林甫使慎矜與御史中丞王□、京兆府法曹吉溫共鞫之。

translations.literal: Jian and Weiming were cast into prison; Linfu had Shenjing, together with Censor-in-Chief Wang Yue and Legal Officer Ji Wen of the Metropolitan Prefecture, jointly interrogate them.
translations.idiomatic: Jian and Weiming were imprisoned; Linfu had Shenjing, Censor-in-Chief Wang Yue, and metropolitan legal officer Ji Wen interrogate them together.

sentences.zh: 上亦疑堅與惟明有謀而不顯其罪，癸酉，下制，責堅以干進不已，貶縉雲太守；

translations.literal: The emperor also suspected Jian and Weiming of plotting but did not make their crime manifest; on the day guiyou he issued a decree, rebuking Jian for ceaseless scheming for advancement and demoting him to Prefect of Jinyun;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also suspected a plot but did not state it openly; on guiyou day he issued a decree rebuking Jian for relentless ambition and demoting him to prefect of Jinyun;

sentences.zh: 惟明以離間君臣，貶播川太守；

translations.literal: Weiming, for sowing division between ruler and minister, was demoted to Prefect of Bo River;
translations.idiomatic: Weiming was demoted to prefect of Bo River for sowing division between ruler and minister;

sentences.zh: 仍別下制戒百官。

translations.literal: and a separate decree was additionally issued to warn the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: and a separate decree warned all officials.

sentences.zh: 以王忠嗣為河西、隴右節度使，兼知朔方、河東節度事。

translations.literal: Wang Zhongsi was made military commissioner of Hexi and Longyou and additionally placed in charge of the military affairs of Shuofang and Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhongsi was made commissioner of Hexi and Longyou and also given charge of Shuofang and Hedong.

sentences.zh: 忠嗣始在朔方、河東，每互市，高估馬價，諸胡聞之，爭賣馬於唐，忠嗣皆買之。

translations.literal: When Zhongsi was first in Shuofang and Hedong, at each frontier market he set a high valuation on horses; the various Hu heard of it and vied to sell horses to Tang, and Zhongsi bought them all.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongsi was first in Shuofang and Hedong, he bid high at frontier markets; the nomads rushed to sell horses to the Tang, and he bought them all.

sentences.zh: 由是胡馬少，唐兵益壯。

translations.literal: By this the Hu had few horses and Tang troops grew still stronger.
translations.idiomatic: The nomads were left with few horses, and Tang forces grew stronger.

sentences.zh: 及徙隴右、河西，復請分朔方、河東馬九千匹以實之，其軍亦壯。

translations.literal: When he was transferred to Longyou and Hexi, he again requested that nine thousand horses from Shuofang and Hedong be divided out to fill his commands; those armies too grew strong.
translations.idiomatic: When he moved to Longyou and Hexi, he secured nine thousand horses from Shuofang and Hedong to fill his commands, and those armies too were strengthened.

sentences.zh: 忠嗣杖四節，控制萬里，天下勁兵重鎮，皆在掌握，與吐蕃戰於青海、積石，皆大捷。

translations.literal: Zhongsi wielded four frontier commissions, controlling ten thousand li; the empire's crack troops and key strongholds were all in his grasp; he fought Tibet at Qinghai and Jishi and in each case won a great victory.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongsi held four frontier commands and controlled ten thousand li; the empire's best troops and key garrisons were in his hands; he fought Tibet at Qinghai and Jishi and won great victories.

sentences.zh: 又討吐谷渾於墨離軍，虜其全部而歸。

translations.literal: He also campaigned against the Tuyuhun at Moli Army, captured their entire tribe, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He also campaigned against the Tuyuhun at Moli Army, captured their entire tribe, and returned.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，癸未，立奚酋娑固為昭信王，契丹酋楷洛為恭仁王。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the day guiwei, the Xi chief Suo Gu was established as King of Zhaoxin, and the Khitan chief Kailuo as King of Gongren.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on guiwei day, the Xi chief Suo Gu was made King of Zhaoxin and the Khitan chief Kailuo King of Gongren.

sentences.zh: 己亥，制：「自今四孟月，皆擇吉日祀天地、九宮。」

translations.literal: On the day jihai, a decree stated, "From now on, in each of the four first months of the seasons, auspicious days shall be chosen to sacrifice to Heaven and Earth and the Nine Palaces."
translations.idiomatic: On jihai day a decree ordered, "From now on, in each of the four seasonal first months, auspicious days shall be chosen to sacrifice to Heaven and Earth and the Nine Palaces."

sentences.zh: 韋堅等既貶，左相李適之懼，自求散地。

translations.literal: After Wei Jian and others had been demoted, Left Chancellor Li Shizhi was afraid and himself sought a post in the provinces.
translations.idiomatic: After Wei Jian and the others were demoted, Left Chancellor Li Shizhi grew afraid and asked for a provincial post.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，以適之為太子少保，罷政事。

translations.literal: On the day gengyin, Shizhi was made Junior Mentor of the Crown Prince and removed from government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin day Shizhi was made junior mentor of the crown prince and removed from government.

sentences.zh: 其子衛尉少卿霅嘗盛饌召客，客畏李林甫，竟日無一人敢往者。

translations.literal: His son Zha, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Guards, once set out a lavish feast and summoned guests; the guests feared Li Linfu, and throughout the day not a single person dared go.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zha, vice director of the court of imperial guards, once gave a lavish banquet; guests feared Li Linfu, and not one dared attend all day.

sentences.zh: 以門下侍郎、崇玄館大學士陳希烈同平章事。

translations.literal: Chen Xilie, Vice Director of the Chancellery and Grand Academician of the Chongxuan Hall, was made Fellow Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xilie, vice director of the chancellery and grand academician of the Chongxuan Hall, was made fellow grand councillor.

sentences.zh: 希烈，宋州人，以講老、莊得進，專用神仙符瑞取媚於上。

translations.literal: Xilie was a man of Song Prefecture; he advanced by lecturing on Laozi and Zhuangzi and relied exclusively on immortals, talismans, and auspicious omens to win favor with the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Xilie came from Song Prefecture; he rose by lecturing on Laozi and Zhuangzi and curried favor with omens of immortality and heavenly portents.

sentences.zh: 李林甫以希烈為上所愛，且柔佞易制，故引以為相；

translations.literal: Li Linfu, because Xilie was loved by the emperor and was moreover soft, fawning, and easy to control, therefore brought him in as chancellor;
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu made him chancellor because the emperor favored him and he was pliable, fawning, and easy to control;

sentences.zh: 凡政事一決於林甫，希烈但給唯諾。

translations.literal: all government affairs were decided solely by Linfu, and Xilie only gave yeses and nos.
translations.idiomatic: all policy was decided by Linfu alone, and Xilie only assented.

sentences.zh: 故事，宰相午後六刻乃出。

translations.literal: By precedent, chancellors did not leave until the sixth quarter after noon.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent chancellors did not leave the office until mid-afternoon.

sentences.zh: 林甫奏，今太平無事，巳時即還第，軍國機務皆決於私家；

translations.literal: Linfu memorialized that now, under great peace and without trouble, he returned to his mansion at the si hour; military and state secrets were all decided in his private residence;
translations.idiomatic: Linfu memorialized that in this age of peace he returned home at mid-morning and decided all military and state affairs at his private residence;

sentences.zh: 主書抱成案詣希烈書名而已。

translations.literal: chief clerks would carry completed dossiers to Xilie for nothing more than signing their names.
translations.idiomatic: chief clerks merely brought completed dossiers for Xilie to sign.

sentences.zh: 五月，壬子朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the first day of the month renzi, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the renzi new moon, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，以劍南節度使章仇兼瓊為戶部尚書；

translations.literal: On the day yihai, Zhang Qiu Jianqiong, military commissioner of Jiannan, was made Minister of Revenue;
translations.idiomatic: On yihai day Jiannan commissioner Zhang Qiu Jianqiong was made minister of revenue;

sentences.zh: 諸楊引之也。

translations.literal: the various Yangs had recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: the Yang clan had recommended him.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，丙辰，敕：「流貶人多在道逗留。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the day bingchen, an edict stated, "Many of those exiled and banished linger on the road.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on bingchen day an edict declared, "Many exiles linger on the road.

sentences.zh: 自今左降官日馳十驛以上。」

translations.literal: From now on demoted officials shall travel ten or more post-stages per day."
translations.idiomatic: From now on demoted officials must travel at least ten post-stages a day."

sentences.zh: 是後流貶者多不全矣。

translations.literal: Thereafter many of those exiled and banished did not survive intact.
translations.idiomatic: After that many exiles did not survive the journey.

sentences.zh: 楊貴妃方有寵，每乘馬則高力士執轡授鞭，織繡之工專供貴妃院者七百人，中外爭獻器服珍玩。

translations.literal: Noble Consort Yang had just won favor; whenever she rode a horse Gao Lishi held the reins and handed her the whip; seven hundred weaving and embroidery craftsmen were devoted exclusively to supplying the Noble Consort's courtyard, and within and without the court vied to present vessels, garments, and rare curios.
translations.idiomatic: Noble Consort Yang was at the height of favor; whenever she rode, Gao Lishi held her reins and handed her the whip; seven hundred weavers and embroiderers served her courtyard alone, and the court and the realm competed to offer her luxuries.

sentences.zh: 嶺南經略使張九章，廣陵長史王翼，以所獻精美，九章加三品，翼入為戶部侍郎；

translations.literal: Lingnan Military Commissioner Zhang Jiuzhang and Yangzhou Chief Administrator Wang Yi, because what they presented was exquisite, received for Jiuzhang promotion by three ranks and for Yi entry into office as Vice Minister of Revenue;
translations.idiomatic: Lingnan commissioner Zhang Jiuzhang and Yangzhou chief administrator Wang Yi, whose tribute was judged finest, were promoted three ranks and made vice minister of revenue respectively;

sentences.zh: 天下從風而靡。

translations.literal: all under Heaven followed the wind and were swept along.
translations.idiomatic: the whole empire rushed to follow suit.

sentences.zh: 民間歌之曰：「生男勿喜女勿悲，君今看女作門楣。」

translations.literal: The common people sang of it, saying, "If you bear a son, do not rejoice; if you bear a daughter, do not grieve—see how today a daughter becomes the lintel of the gate."
translations.idiomatic: A popular song ran, "Do not rejoice at a son or grieve at a daughter—see how a daughter now becomes the lintel of the house."

sentences.zh: 妃欲得生荔支，歲命嶺南馳驛致之。

translations.literal: The consort wished to have fresh lychees; each year she ordered Lingnan to dispatch them by urgent relay.
translations.idiomatic: The consort wanted fresh lychees, and each year ordered them rushed from Lingnan by relay.

sentences.zh: 比至長安，色味不變。

translations.literal: By the time they reached Chang'an, color and flavor were unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached Chang'an, their color and flavor were unchanged.

sentences.zh: 至是，妃以妒悍不遜，上怒，命送歸兄銛之第。

translations.literal: At this time the consort, for jealousy, fierceness, and lack of deference, angered the emperor, who ordered her sent back to the mansion of her elder brother Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Then the consort's jealous temper offended the emperor, who ordered her sent to her brother Xian's house.

sentences.zh: 是日，上不懌，比日中，猶未食。

translations.literal: That day the emperor was displeased; by midday he still had not eaten.
translations.idiomatic: That day the emperor was out of sorts and had not eaten by noon.

sentences.zh: 左右動不稱旨，橫被棰撻。

translations.literal: Those at his side, whenever they failed to suit his intent, were beaten with clubs without cause.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants who displeased him were beaten without cause.

sentences.zh: 高力士欲嘗上意，請悉載院中儲偫送貴妃，凡百餘車；

translations.literal: Gao Lishi wished to test the emperor's mind and asked to load all the stored provisions of the courtyard and send them to the Noble Consort—more than a hundred carts in all;
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lishi, testing the emperor's mood, asked to send all the consort's stored goods from her courtyard—more than a hundred cartloads;

sentences.zh: 上自分御膳以賜之。

translations.literal: the emperor himself divided his imperial meal to bestow it on her.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor himself sent portions of his own meal as a gift.

sentences.zh: 及夜，力士伏奏請迎貴妃歸院，遂開禁門而入。

translations.literal: When night came, Lishi submitted from his kneeling position asking to welcome the Noble Consort back to the courtyard; the forbidden gate was then opened and she entered.
translations.idiomatic: That night Lishi knelt and asked to bring the Noble Consort back; the forbidden gate was opened and she entered the palace.

sentences.zh: 自是恩遇愈隆，後宮莫得進矣。

translations.literal: From then on favor and treatment grew still more lofty, and none in the inner palace could advance.
translations.idiomatic: From then on her favor only grew, and no other woman of the inner palace could approach her.

sentences.zh: 將作少匠韋蘭、兵部員外郎韋芝為其兄堅訟冤，且引太子為言；

translations.literal: Wei Lan, Vice Director of Palace Construction, and Wei Zhi, Ministry of War Outside-the-Regular Attendant, pleaded their elder brother Jian's injustice and moreover cited the Crown Prince in their words;
translations.idiomatic: Wei Lan, vice director of palace construction, and Wei Zhi, Ministry of War outside attendant, petitioned for their brother Jian and invoked the crown prince;

sentences.zh: 上益怒。

translations.literal: the emperor grew still angrier.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor grew angrier still.

sentences.zh: 太子懼，表請與妃離婚，乞不以親廢法。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince was afraid and submitted a memorial requesting divorce from his consort, begging that kinship not cause the law to be set aside.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince, in fear, memorialized to divorce his consort and begged that kinship not override the law.

sentences.zh: 丙子，再貶堅江夏別駕，蘭、芝皆貶嶺南。

translations.literal: On the day bingzi, Jian was again demoted to Vice Prefect of Jiangxia; Lan and Zhi were both banished to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi day Jian was demoted again to vice prefect of Jiangxia; Lan and Zhi were both sent to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 然上素知太子孝謹，故譴怒不及。

translations.literal: Yet the emperor had long known the Crown Prince to be filial and cautious, and therefore his rebuke and anger did not reach him.
translations.idiomatic: But the emperor had long known the crown prince to be dutiful and careful, and his wrath did not touch him.

sentences.zh: 李林甫因言堅與李適之等為朋黨，後數日，堅長流臨封，適之貶宜春太守，太常少卿韋斌貶巴陵太守，嗣薛王琄貶夷陵別駕，睢陽太守裴寬貶安陸別駕，河南尹李齊物貶竟陵太守，凡堅親黨連坐流貶者數十人。

translations.literal: Li Linfu thereupon said that Jian and Li Shizhi and others formed a faction; several days later Jian was exiled far to Linfeng, Shizhi was demoted to Prefect of Yichun, Wei Bin, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, to Prefect of Baling, Heir of Prince Xue Juan to Vice Prefect of Yiling, Pei Kuan, Prefect of Suiyang, to Vice Prefect of Anlu, Li Qiwu, Prefect of Henan, to Prefect of Jingling—in all, several tens among Jian's kin and associates suffered joint punishment of exile and demotion.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu then accused Jian, Li Shizhi, and others of forming a faction; days later Jian was exiled to Linfeng, Shizhi to prefect of Yichun, Wei Bin to prefect of Baling, Heir of Prince Xue Juan to vice prefect of Yiling, Pei Kuan to vice prefect of Anlu, and Li Qiwu to prefect of Jingling—dozens of Jian's kin and associates in all.

sentences.zh: 斌，安石之子。

translations.literal: Bin was the son of Anshi.
translations.idiomatic: Bin was the son of Wei Anshi.

sentences.zh: 琄，業之子，堅之甥也。

translations.literal: Juan was the son of Ye and Jian's nephew by marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Juan was Ye's son and Jian's nephew by marriage.

sentences.zh: 琄母亦令隨琄之官。

translations.literal: Juan's mother was also ordered to follow Juan to his post.
translations.idiomatic: Juan's mother was also ordered to accompany him to his post.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，戊戌，上幸驪山溫泉；

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the day wuxu, the emperor visited Mount Li hot springs;
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on wuxu day, the emperor went to the hot springs at Mount Li;

sentences.zh: 十一月，乙巳，還宮。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the day yisi, he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on yisi day, he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 贊善大夫杜有鄰，女為太子良娣，良娣之姊為左驍衛兵曹柳勣妻。

translations.literal: Palace Companion Du Youlin's daughter was a senior consort of the Crown Prince; the senior consort's elder sister was wife to Liu Ji, military staff officer of the Left Agile Cavalry Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Palace companion Du Youlin's daughter was a senior consort of the crown prince; her elder sister was married to Liu Ji, staff officer of the Left Agile Cavalry Guard.

sentences.zh: 勣性狂疏，好功名，喜交結豪俊。

translations.literal: Ji was by nature wild and careless, fond of fame and merit, and delighted to befriend bold and outstanding men.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was reckless and ambitious, eager for renown, and fond of befriending bold men.

sentences.zh: 淄川太守裴敦復薦於北海太守李邕，邕與之定交。

translations.literal: Zichuan Prefect Pei Dunfu recommended him to Beihai Prefect Li Yong, and Yong formed a sworn friendship with him.
translations.idiomatic: Zichuan prefect Pei Dunfu recommended him to Beihai prefect Li Yong, who became his close friend.

sentences.zh: 勣至京師，與著作郎王曾等為友，皆當時名士也。

translations.literal: When Ji reached the capital he befriended Wang Zeng, Master of Writings, and others—all famed men of the age.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital Ji befriended Master of Writings Wang Zeng and other celebrated men of the day.

sentences.zh: 勣與妻族不協，欲陷之，為飛語，告有鄰妄稱圖讖，交構東宮，指斥乘輿。

translations.literal: Ji was not in harmony with his wife's kin and wished to entrap them; he spread whispered slander, reporting that Youlin had falsely invoked prognostic texts, plotted against the Eastern Palace, and reviled the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Ji quarreled with his wife's family and sought to destroy them; he spread slander accusing Youlin of false prophecy, plotting against the Eastern Palace, and insulting the throne.

sentences.zh: 林甫令京兆士曹吉溫與御史鞫之，乃勣首謀也。

translations.literal: Linfu had Metropolitan Staff Officer Ji Wen and a censor interrogate the case; it turned out that Ji was the chief plotter.
translations.idiomatic: Linfu had metropolitan staff officer Ji Wen and a censor investigate; Ji himself was the chief plotter.

sentences.zh: 溫令勣連引曾等入台。

translations.literal: Wen had Ji implicate Zeng and others in succession and bring them into the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Wen made Ji implicate Zeng and the others and bring them before the censorate.

sentences.zh: 十二月，甲戌，有鄰、勣及曾等皆杖死，積屍大理，妻子流遠方；

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day jiaxu, Youlin, Ji, Zeng, and the others were all beaten to death; corpses piled up at the Court of Judicial Review, and wives and children were exiled to distant regions;
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on jiaxu day, Youlin, Ji, Zeng, and the rest were all beaten to death; bodies piled up at the Court of Judicial Review, and their families were exiled;

sentences.zh: 中外震慄。

translations.literal: within and without the court there was trembling fear.
translations.idiomatic: Court and realm were shaken with terror.

sentences.zh: 嗣虢王巨貶義陽司馬。

translations.literal: Heir of Prince Guo Ju was demoted to Militia Commander of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Heir of Prince Guo Ju was demoted to militia commander of Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 巨，邕之子也。

translations.literal: Ju was Yong's son.
translations.idiomatic: Ju was Li Yong's son.

sentences.zh: 別遣監察御史羅希奭往按李邕，太子亦出良娣為庶人。

translations.literal: A separate commission sent Attending Investigative Censor Luo Xiyi to investigate Li Yong; the Crown Prince also demoted his senior consort to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: Attending investigative censor Luo Xiyi was separately sent to investigate Li Yong; the crown prince also demoted his senior consort to commoner.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，鄴郡太守王琚坐贓貶江華司馬。

translations.literal: On the day yihai, Ye Prefect Wang Ju, charged with corruption, was demoted to Militia Commander of Jianghua.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai day Ye prefect Wang Ju was demoted to militia commander of Jianghua on corruption charges.

sentences.zh: 琚性豪侈，與李邕皆自謂耆舊，久在外，意怏怏，李林甫惡其負材使氣，故因事除之。

translations.literal: Ju was by nature extravagant; he and Li Yong both called themselves elders of long service; long abroad, they were discontent in mind; Li Linfu hated them for relying on talent and venting their spirit, and therefore used the affair to remove them.
translations.idiomatic: Ju was extravagant; he and Li Yong considered themselves elder statesmen and, long abroad, were resentful; Li Linfu hated their pride and used the affair to destroy them.

sentences.zh: 玄宗至道大聖大明孝皇帝中之下天寶六年（

translations.literal: Middle-lower portion of the reign of Emperor Xuanzong, Sagacious Emperor of the Supreme Way, Great Brightness, and Filial Piety—Tianbao year 6 (
translations.idiomatic: Middle-lower portion of the reign of Emperor Xuanzong of the Tang—Tianbao year 6 (

sentences.zh: 丁亥，公元七四七年）

translations.literal: dinghai, corresponding to the year 747 CE)
translations.idiomatic: dinghai, AD 747)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛巳。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the day xinsi.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on xinsi day.

sentences.zh: 李邕、裴敦復皆杖死。

translations.literal: Li Yong and Pei Dunfu were both beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yong and Pei Dunfu were both beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 邕才藝出眾，盧藏用常語之曰：「君如干將、莫邪，難與爭鋒，然終虞缺折耳。」

translations.literal: Yong's talent and artistry were outstanding; Lu Zangyong often said to him, "You are like Ganjiang and Moye—hard to contend with in the edge of the blade, yet in the end one must fear a chip or break."
translations.idiomatic: Yong's talent was extraordinary; Lu Zangyong once told him, "You are like the swords Ganjiang and Moye—none can match your edge, yet you will break in the end."

sentences.zh: 邕不能用。

translations.literal: Yong could not apply this.
translations.idiomatic: Yong would not heed the warning.

sentences.zh: 林甫又奏分遣御史即貶所賜皇甫惟明、韋堅兄弟等死。

translations.literal: Linfu again memorialized to dispatch censors separately to the places of exile to grant death to Huangfu Weiming, the brothers of Wei Jian, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Linfu memorialized again to send censors to the places of exile to order the deaths of Huangfu Weiming, Wei Jian's brothers, and others.

sentences.zh: 羅殺奭自青州如嶺南，所過殺遷謫者，郡縣惶駭。

translations.literal: Luo Sha'yi went from Qingzhou toward Lingnan; wherever he passed he killed those under banishment and transfer, and commanderies and counties were struck with fear.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Sha'yi left Qingzhou for Lingnan, killing exiles wherever he passed, and commanderies and counties were terrified.

sentences.zh: 排馬牒至宜春，李適之憂懼，仰藥自殺。

translations.literal: When the urgent dispatch arrived at Yichun, Li Shizhi, anxious and afraid, took poison and killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: When the urgent dispatch reached Yichun, Li Shizhi took poison and killed himself in dread.

sentences.zh: 至江華，王琚仰藥不死，聞希奭已至，即自縊。

translations.literal: When he reached Jianghua, Wang Ju took poison but did not die; hearing that Xi'yi had arrived, he immediately hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: At Jianghua Wang Ju took poison but survived; hearing Xiyi had arrived, he hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 希奭又迂路過安陸，欲怖殺裴寬，寬向希奭叩頭祈生，希奭不宿而過，乃得免。

translations.literal: Xi'yi again took a detour through Anlu, intending to terrify Pei Kuan to death; Kuan kowtowed to Xi'yi begging for his life; Xi'yi did not lodge but passed on, and Kuan thereby escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyi detoured through Anlu intending to frighten Pei Kuan to death; Kuan kowtowed begging for his life; Xiyi did not stay the night but passed on, and Kuan was spared.

sentences.zh: 李適之子適迎父喪至東京，李林甫令人誣告適，杖死於河南府。

translations.literal: Li Shizhi's son Shi met his father's funeral bier at the Eastern Capital; Li Linfu had a man lodge a false accusation against Shi, and he was beaten to death in the Henan prefectural office.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shizhi's son Shi met his father's funeral at the Eastern Capital; Li Linfu had him falsely accused and beaten to death in the Henan prefectural office.

sentences.zh: 給事中房琯坐與適之善，貶宜春太守。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Fang Guan, charged with friendship with Shizhi, was demoted to Prefect of Yichun.
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendant Fang Guan, charged with friendship with Shizhi, was demoted to prefect of Yichun.

sentences.zh: 琯，融之子也。

translations.literal: Guan was the son of Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Guan was the son of Fang Rong.

sentences.zh: 林甫恨韋堅不已，遣使於循河及江、淮州縣求堅罪，所在收系綱典船夫，溢於牢獄，征剝逋負，延及鄰伍，皆裸露死於公府，至林甫薨乃止。

translations.literal: Linfu hated Wei Jian without cease and sent envoys to the Xun River and to prefectures and counties of the Jiang and Huai to seek crimes of Jian's; wherever they went they seized and imprisoned ferry masters and boatmen until the prisons overflowed, exacted and stripped overdue payments, extending even to neighboring households—all died naked in the government offices, and only when Linfu died did it stop.
translations.idiomatic: Linfu never ceased hating Wei Jian and sent agents along the Xun River and the Jiang and Huai to hunt for crimes; they imprisoned ferry masters and boatmen until the jails overflowed, extorted debts from neighbors, and left men stripped and dead in government offices—the persecution ended only with Linfu's death.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，上享太廟；

translations.literal: On the day dinghai, the emperor offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple;
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai day the emperor offered at the imperial ancestral temple;

sentences.zh: 戊子，合祭天地於南郊，赦天下。

translations.literal: On the day wuzi, he performed a joint sacrifice to Heaven and Earth at the southern suburb and pardoned all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi day he sacrificed jointly to Heaven and Earth at the southern suburb and issued a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 制免百姓今載田租。

translations.literal: A decree exempted the common people from the land tax of the current era Zai.
translations.idiomatic: A decree exempted the people from the land tax for the current Zai era.

sentences.zh: 又令除削絞、斬條。

translations.literal: It also ordered the abolition and cutting away of the statutes on strangulation and decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: It also abolished the statutes on strangulation and decapitation.

sentences.zh: 上慕好生之名，故令應絞、斬者皆重杖流嶺南，其實有司率杖殺之。

translations.literal: The emperor admired the reputation of cherishing life; therefore he ordered that those who should be strangled or decapitated were all heavily clubbed and exiled to Lingnan—but in fact the responsible offices as a rule clubbed them to death.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to be known as merciful and ordered that those liable to strangulation or decapitation be heavily clubbed and exiled to Lingnan—but in practice the authorities usually beat them to death.

sentences.zh: 又令天下為嫁母服三載。

translations.literal: He also ordered that all under Heaven observe three years of mourning for a mother remarried.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered three years of mourning throughout the realm for a remarried mother.

sentences.zh: 上欲廣求天下之士，命通一藝以上皆詣京師。

translations.literal: The emperor wished broadly to seek men of talent throughout the realm and ordered that all who had mastered one art or more proceed to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to recruit talent broadly and ordered all who had mastered any art to come to the capital.

sentences.zh: 李林甫恐草野之士對策斥言其奸惡，建言：「舉人多卑賤愚聵，恐有俚言污濁聖聽。」

translations.literal: Li Linfu feared that men of the wilds, in answering policy questions, would denounce his wickedness and offered advice: "Those presented for office are mostly base, mean, and stupid and deaf; I fear there may be rustic words that foul and muddy the sage's hearing."
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu feared that commoners answering policy questions would denounce his crimes and advised: "Candidates are mostly base and ignorant; rustic speech may offend the imperial ear."

sentences.zh: 乃令郡縣長官精加試練，灼然超絕者，具名送省，委尚書覆試，御史中丞監之，取名實相副者聞奏。

translations.literal: He therefore ordered prefectural and county chiefs to test and drill them with care; those clearly and outstandingly superior were to have their names listed and sent to the province, entrusted to the Ministry of Revenue for re-examination with the Censor-in-Chief supervising, and only those whose names and realities matched were to be reported to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered local officials to test candidates carefully and send only the truly outstanding to the capital for re-examination under the censor-in-chief's supervision, reporting to the throne only those who proved worthy.

sentences.zh: 既而至者皆試以詩、賦、論，遂無一人及第者，林甫乃上表賀野無遺賢。

translations.literal: When those who arrived were all tested with poetry, rhapsodies, and discourses, in the end not a single person passed the examination; Linfu thereupon submitted a memorial congratulating the wilds on having no talent left neglected.
translations.idiomatic: When the arrivals were tested in poetry, rhapsody, and discourse, not one passed; Linfu then memorialized to congratulate the emperor that no talent remained hidden in the realm.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，以范陽、平盧節度使安祿山兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: On the day wuyin, An Lushan, military commissioner of Fanyang and Pinglu, was additionally made Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin day An Lushan, commissioner of Fanyang and Pinglu, was also made censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 祿山體充肥，腹垂過膝，嘗自稱重三百斤。

translations.literal: Lushan's body was full and fat; his belly hung down past his knees, and he once declared his own weight to be three hundred jin.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan was enormously fat; his belly hung below his knees, and he claimed to weigh three hundred jin.

sentences.zh: 外若癡直，內實狡黠。

translations.literal: Outwardly he seemed dull and blunt; inwardly he was in truth crafty and cunning.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly he seemed dull and blunt; inwardly he was crafty and cunning.

sentences.zh: 常令其將劉駱谷留京師詗朝廷指趣，動靜皆報之。

translations.literal: He regularly had his general Liu Luogu remain in the capital to spy out the court's intentions and trends, reporting all movements.
translations.idiomatic: He kept his general Liu Luogu in the capital to spy on the court and report every move.

sentences.zh: 或應有箋表者，駱谷即為代作通之。

translations.literal: When memorials or reports were needed, Luogu would compose them on his behalf and pass them through.
translations.idiomatic: When memorials were needed, Luogu drafted and submitted them for him.

sentences.zh: 歲獻俘虜、雜畜、奇禽、異獸、珍玩之物，不絕於路，郡縣疲於遞運。

translations.literal: Each year he presented captives, miscellaneous livestock, rare birds, exotic beasts, and precious curios; the gifts were unceasing on the roads, and commanderies and counties were worn out by relay transport.
translations.idiomatic: Each year he sent captives, livestock, rare birds and beasts, and curios without end; commanderies and counties were exhausted by relay transport.

sentences.zh: 祿山在上前，應對敏給，雜以詼諧。

translations.literal: Before the emperor Lushan answered swiftly and readily, mixing in wit and humor.
translations.idiomatic: In the emperor's presence Lushan answered swiftly and wittily.

sentences.zh: 上嘗戲指其腹曰：「此胡腹中何所有，其大乃爾！」

translations.literal: The emperor once playfully pointed at his belly and said, "What is inside this barbarian's belly, that it is so large!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once joked, pointing at his belly, "What is inside this barbarian's belly that it is so huge!"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「更無餘物，正有赤心耳！」

translations.literal: He replied, "Nothing else at all—only a loyal red heart!"
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Nothing else—only a loyal heart!"

sentences.zh: 上悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted.

sentences.zh: 又嘗命見太子，祿山不拜。

translations.literal: On another occasion he ordered him to be received by the Crown Prince; Lushan did not bow.
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion he was presented to the crown prince; Lushan did not bow.

sentences.zh: 左右趣之拜，祿山拱立曰：「臣胡人，不習朝儀，不知太子者何官？」

translations.literal: Those at his side urged him to bow; Lushan stood with clasped hands and said, "Your subject is a barbarian, unversed in court ritual—I do not know what office the Crown Prince holds?"
translations.idiomatic: Attendants urged him to bow; Lushan stood with clasped hands and said, "I am a barbarian, unversed in court ritual—what office is the crown prince?"

sentences.zh: 上曰：「此儲君也，朕千秋萬歲後，代朕君汝者也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "This is the heir apparent; after I live ten thousand years and ten thousand autumns, he will rule you in my place."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "This is the heir apparent; when I am gone he will rule you in my place."

sentences.zh: 祿山曰：「臣愚，向者惟知有陛下一人，不知乃更有儲君。」

translations.literal: Lushan said, "Your subject is foolish; formerly I knew only that there was Your Majesty alone—I did not know there was also an heir apparent."
translations.idiomatic: Lushan said, "I am foolish; I knew only Your Majesty—I did not know there was also an heir apparent."

sentences.zh: 不得已，然後拜。

translations.literal: Only when he had no choice did he then bow.
translations.idiomatic: Only then, with no choice, did he bow.

sentences.zh: 上以為信然，益愛之。

translations.literal: The emperor considered this sincere and loved him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took this as sincere and loved him all the more.

sentences.zh: 上嘗宴勤政樓，百官列坐樓下，獨為祿山於御座東間設金雞障，置榻使坐其前，仍命捲簾以示榮寵。

translations.literal: The emperor once gave a banquet at the Diligence in Government Tower; the hundred officials sat in ranks below the tower, but for Lushan alone he set up a golden-cock screen in the eastern bay of the imperial seat, placed a couch for him to sit before it, and still ordered the curtain rolled up to display honor and favor.
translations.idiomatic: At a banquet in the Diligence in Government Tower, officials sat below while Lushan alone was given a golden-cock screen east of the throne, a couch before it, and the curtain raised to display imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 命楊銛、楊錡、貴妃三姊皆與祿山敘兄弟。

translations.literal: He ordered Yang Xian, Yang Qi, and the Noble Consort's three elder sisters all to treat Lushan as sworn brothers.
translations.idiomatic: He had Yang Xian, Yang Qi, and the Noble Consort's three elder sisters swear brotherhood with Lushan.

sentences.zh: 祿山得出入禁中，因請為貴妃兒。

translations.literal: Lushan was allowed to enter and leave the forbidden precincts and thereupon asked to become the Noble Consort's son.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan was allowed free access to the inner palace and asked to become the Noble Consort's adopted son.

sentences.zh: 上與貴妃共坐，祿山先拜貴妃。

translations.literal: The emperor and the Noble Consort sat together; Lushan bowed first to the Noble Consort.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor and Noble Consort sat together, Lushan bowed first to the consort.

sentences.zh: 上問何故，對曰：「胡人先母而後父。」

translations.literal: The emperor asked why; he replied, "Barbarians honor the mother before the father."
translations.idiomatic: Asked why, he said, "Barbarians honor the mother before the father."

sentences.zh: 上悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted.

sentences.zh: 李林甫以王忠嗣功名日盛，恐其入相，忌之。

translations.literal: Li Linfu, because Wang Zhongsi's fame and achievement grew daily, feared he might enter the chancellorship and was jealous of him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu, fearing Wang Zhongsi's rising fame might bring him to the chancellorship, envied him.

sentences.zh: 安祿山潛蓄異志，托以禦寇，築雄武城，大貯兵器，請忠嗣助役，因欲留其兵。

translations.literal: An Lushan secretly harbored a different intent; under the pretext of defending against invaders he built Xiongwu City, stored weapons in great quantity, asked Zhongsi to help with the labor, and thereby wished to detain his troops.
translations.idiomatic: An Lushan secretly harbored rebellion; under pretext of defense he built Xiongwu City, stockpiled weapons, asked Zhongsi to help with labor, and hoped to keep his troops.

sentences.zh: 忠嗣先期而往，不見祿山而還，數上言祿山必反；

translations.literal: Zhongsi went ahead on schedule, did not see Lushan, and returned; he repeatedly memorialized that Lushan would surely rebel;
translations.idiomatic: Zhongsi went early, found Lushan absent, and returned; he repeatedly warned that Lushan would rebel;

sentences.zh: 林甫益惡之。

translations.literal: and Linfu hated him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: and Linfu hated him all the more.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，忠嗣固辭兼河東、朔方節度；

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Zhongsi firmly declined the additional commands of Hedong and Shuofang;
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, Zhongsi firmly declined the additional commands of Hedong and Shuofang;

sentences.zh: 許之。

translations.literal: The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: His request was granted.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，己酉，上幸驪山溫泉，改溫泉宮曰華清宮。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the day jiyou, the emperor visited Mount Li hot springs and changed the name of the Hot Spring Palace to Huaqing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on jiyou day, the emperor went to the Mount Li hot springs and renamed the Hot Spring Palace Huaqing Palace.

sentences.zh: 河西、隴右節度使王忠嗣以部將哥舒翰為大斗副使，李光弼為河西兵馬使，充赤水軍使。

translations.literal: Wang Zhongsi, military commissioner of Hexi and Longyou, made his subordinate general Geshu Han deputy commander of Dadou, and Li Guangbi military commissioner of Hexi, filling the post of commander of the Chishui Army.
translations.idiomatic: Hexi and Longyou commissioner Wang Zhongsi made Geshu Han deputy commander of Dadou and Li Guangbi Hexi military commissioner and commander of the Chishui Army.

sentences.zh: 翰父祖本突騎施別部酋長，光弼，契丹王楷洛之子也，皆以勇略為忠嗣所重。

translations.literal: Han's father and grandfather had originally been chiefs of a separate branch of the Turgesh; Guangbi was the son of the Khitan king Kailuo—all were valued by Zhongsi for courage and strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Han's forebears were Turgesh chiefs; Guangbi was son of the Khitan king Kailuo—Zhongsi valued both for courage and strategy.

sentences.zh: 忠嗣使翰擊吐蕃，有同列為之副，倨慢不為用，翰撾殺之，軍中股心栗；

translations.literal: Zhongsi had Han attack Tibet; a colleague served as his deputy, was arrogant and slow and would not obey; Han beat him to death, and in the army thighs trembled with fear;
translations.idiomatic: Zhongsi sent Han against Tibet; a deputy was arrogant and disobedient, and Han beat him to death—the army shook with terror;

sentences.zh: 累功至隴右節度副使。

translations.literal: through accumulated merit he rose to Vice Commissioner of Longyou.
translations.idiomatic: through accumulated merit he rose to vice commissioner of Longyou.

sentences.zh: 每歲積石軍麥熟，吐蕃輒來獲之，無能御者，邊人謂之「吐蕃麥莊」。

translations.literal: Every year when the wheat ripened at Jishi Army, Tibet would come and harvest it; none could resist, and border people called it "Tibet's wheat estate."
translations.idiomatic: Each year when wheat ripened at Jishi Army, Tibet harvested it unopposed—borderers called it "Tibet's wheat farm."

sentences.zh: 翰先伏兵於其側，虜至，斷其後，夾擊之，無一人得返者，自是不敢復來。

translations.literal: Han first set ambush troops on the flank; when the enemy arrived he cut off their rear and struck from both sides; not one man returned, and from then on they did not dare come again.
translations.idiomatic: Han ambushed them on the flank, cut off their retreat, and attacked from both sides—not one returned, and they never came again.

sentences.zh: 上欲使王忠嗣攻吐蕃石堡城，忠嗣上言：「石堡險固，吐蕃舉國守之。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to have Wang Zhongsi attack Tibet's Shibao City; Zhongsi memorialized, "Shibao is perilous and strong, and Tibet guards it with the whole state.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wanted Wang Zhongsi to attack Tibet's Shibao City; Zhongsi memorialized, "Shibao is formidable and Tibet defends it with the whole nation.

sentences.zh: 今頓兵其下，非殺數萬人不能克。

translations.literal: To encamp troops beneath it now would require killing tens of thousands before it could be taken.
translations.idiomatic: To camp beneath it now would cost tens of thousands of lives.

sentences.zh: 臣恐所得不如所亡，不如且厲兵秣馬，俟其有釁，然後取之。」

translations.literal: Your subject fears the gain would not equal the loss; it would be better for the time being to sharpen the troops and feed the horses, wait until they show a crack, and then take it."
translations.idiomatic: The gain would not repay the cost; better to train the army and wait for an opening."

sentences.zh: 上意不快。

translations.literal: The emperor's mind was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 將軍董延光自請將兵取石堡城，上命忠嗣分兵助之。

translations.literal: General Dong Yanguang volunteered to lead troops to take Shibao City; the emperor ordered Zhongsi to divide forces and assist him.
translations.idiomatic: General Dong Yanguang volunteered to take Shibao; the emperor ordered Zhongsi to send supporting troops.

sentences.zh: 忠嗣不得已奉詔，而不盡副延光所欲，延光怨之。

translations.literal: Zhongsi, having no choice, obeyed the edict but did not fully supply all that Yanguang desired; Yanguang resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongsi obeyed but did not give Yanguang everything he wanted; Yanguang resented him.

sentences.zh: 李光弼言於忠嗣曰：「大夫以愛士卒之故，不欲成延光之功，雖迫於制書，實奪其謀也。

translations.literal: Li Guangbi said to Zhongsi, "The Grand Master, out of love for the soldiers, does not wish to complete Yanguang's achievement; though compelled by imperial order, in truth you are thwarting his plan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangbi told Zhongsi, "You will not complete Yanguang's victory out of love for your men; though compelled by order, you are thwarting his plan.

sentences.zh: 何以知之？

translations.literal: How do I know this?
translations.idiomatic: How do I know?

sentences.zh: 今以數萬眾授之而不立重賞，士卒安肯為之盡力乎！

translations.literal: Now you give him tens of thousands of men but set no heavy rewards—how will the soldiers be willing to exert themselves to the full for him!
translations.idiomatic: You give him tens of thousands of men but offer no great rewards—how will they fight their hardest!

sentences.zh: 然此天子意也，彼無功，必歸罪於大夫。

translations.literal: Yet this is the Son of Heaven's intent; if he has no success, he will surely lay the blame on the Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: Yet this is the emperor's wish; if Yanguang fails, he will blame you.

sentences.zh: 大夫軍府充牣，何愛數萬段帛不以杜其讒口乎！」

translations.literal: The Grand Master's military headquarters are filled to overflowing—why begrudge tens of thousands of bolts of silk to shut the mouths of slanderers!"
translations.idiomatic: Your headquarters overflow with stores—why not spend tens of thousands of bolts of silk to silence slander!"

sentences.zh: 忠嗣曰：「今以數萬之眾爭一城，得之未足以制敵，不得亦無害於國，故忠嗣不欲為之。

translations.literal: Zhongsi said, "To contend for one city now with tens of thousands of men—if we gain it, it is not enough to control the enemy; if we do not gain it, there is no harm to the state. Therefore Zhongsi does not wish to do it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongsi replied, "To fight for one city with tens of thousands—taking it would not break the enemy, and failing would not harm the state. I will not do it.

sentences.zh: 忠嗣今受責天子，不過以金吾、羽林一將軍歸宿衛，其次不過黔中上佐；

translations.literal: If Zhongsi is now rebuked by the Son of Heaven, at most he returns as a general of the Golden Guard or Feathered Forest to palace guard duty; next below that, at most senior aide in Qianzhong;
translations.idiomatic: If the emperor rebukes me, at worst I return as a Golden Guard or Feathered Forest general; at worst I become a senior aide in Qianzhong;

sentences.zh: 忠嗣豈以數萬人之命易一官乎！

translations.literal: would Zhongsi trade the lives of tens of thousands of men for one office!
translations.idiomatic: would I trade tens of thousands of lives for one post!

sentences.zh: 李將軍，子誠愛我矣，然吾志決矣，子勿復言！」

translations.literal: General Li, you truly love me, yet my resolve is fixed—do not speak again!"
translations.idiomatic: General Li, you truly care for me, but my mind is made up—say no more!"

sentences.zh: 光弼曰：「向者恐為大夫之累，故不敢不言。

translations.literal: Guangbi said, "Earlier I feared becoming a burden to the Grand Master, and therefore did not dare remain silent.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi said, "I spoke because I feared burdening you.

sentences.zh: 今大夫能行古人之事，非光弼所及也。」

translations.literal: Now the Grand Master can act as the ancients did—this is not something Guangbi can match."
translations.idiomatic: Now you act as the ancients did—I cannot match you."

sentences.zh: 遂趨出。

translations.literal: He thereupon hurried out.
translations.idiomatic: He hurried out.

sentences.zh: 延光過期不克，言忠嗣沮撓軍計，上怒。

translations.literal: Yanguang passed the deadline without taking the city and said Zhongsi had obstructed and thwarted the military plan; the emperor was angry.
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang missed his deadline and accused Zhongsi of obstructing the campaign; the emperor was furious.

sentences.zh: 李林甫因使濟陽別駕魏林告「忠嗣嘗自言我幼養宮中，與忠王相愛狎」，欲擁兵以尊奉太子。

translations.literal: Li Linfu thereupon had Jiyang Vice Prefect Wei Lin report, "Zhongsi once said of himself, 'I was raised in the palace in youth and was intimate with Prince Zhong,'" intending to gather troops to honor and support the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu had Jiyang vice prefect Wei Lin report that Zhongsi had said, "I was raised in the palace and was intimate with Prince Zhong," and intended to use troops to support the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 敕征忠嗣入朝，委三司鞫之。

translations.literal: An edict summoned Zhongsi to court and entrusted the Three Offices with interrogating him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict summoned Zhongsi to court and entrusted the Three Offices with his trial.

sentences.zh: 上聞哥舒翰名，召見華清宮，與語，悅之。

translations.literal: The emperor heard Geshu Han's name, summoned him for audience at Huaqing Palace, spoke with him, and was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of Geshu Han, the emperor summoned him to Huaqing Palace, spoke with him, and was pleased.

sentences.zh: 十一月，辛卯，以翰判西平太守，充隴右節度使；

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the day xinmao, Han was made acting Prefect of Xiping and filled the post of military commissioner of Longyou;
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on xinmao day, Han was made acting prefect of Xiping and commissioner of Longyou;

sentences.zh: 以朔方節度使安思順判武威郡事，充河西節度使。

translations.literal: Shuofang Military Commissioner An Sishun was made acting administrator of Wuwei Commandery and filled the post of military commissioner of Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: Shuofang commissioner An Sishun was made acting administrator of Wuwei and commissioner of Hexi.

sentences.zh: 戶部侍郎兼御史中丞楊慎矜為上所厚，李林甫浸忌之。

translations.literal: Yang Shenjing, Vice Minister of Revenue and concurrent Censor-in-Chief, was deeply favored by the emperor; Li Linfu gradually grew jealous of him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shenjing, vice minister of revenue and censor-in-chief, enjoyed the emperor's deep favor; Li Linfu gradually came to envy him.

sentences.zh: 慎矜與王□父晉，中表兄弟也，少與□狎，□之入台，頗因慎矜推引。

translations.literal: Shenjing and Wang Yue's father Jin were cousins; in youth he was intimate with Yue, and when Yue entered the Censorate he had largely been promoted through Shenjing's recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: Shenjing and Wang Yue's father Jin were cousins; Shenjing had been close to Yue in youth and largely secured his entry into the censorate.

sentences.zh: 及□遷中丞，慎矜與語，猶名之；

translations.literal: When Yue was transferred to Censor-in-Chief, Shenjing still addressed him by personal name in conversation;
translations.idiomatic: When Yue became censor-in-chief, Shenjing still addressed him by personal name;

sentences.zh: □自恃與林甫善，意稍不平。

translations.literal: Yue, relying on his friendship with Linfu, was somewhat discontent in mind.
translations.idiomatic: Yue, counting on his friendship with Linfu, grew resentful.

sentences.zh: 慎矜奪□職田，□母本賤，慎矜嘗以語人；

translations.literal: Shenjing seized Yue's official field allotment; Yue's mother had originally been of low status, and Shenjing had once spoken of this to others;
translations.idiomatic: Shenjing seized Yue's official land; Yue's mother had been of low birth, and Shenjing had gossiped about it;

sentences.zh: □深銜之。

translations.literal: Yue bore a deep grievance against him.
translations.idiomatic: Yue deeply resented him.

sentences.zh: 慎矜猶以故意待之，嘗與之私語讖書。

translations.literal: Shenjing still treated him with old affection and once spoke with him in private about prognostic texts.
translations.idiomatic: Shenjing still treated him as an old friend and once discussed prognostic texts with him in private.

sentences.zh: 慎矜與術士史敬忠善，敬忠言天下將亂，勸慎矜於臨汝山中買莊為避亂之所。

translations.literal: Shenjing was on good terms with the technician Shi Jingzhong; Jingzhong said all under Heaven would fall into disorder and urged Shenjing to buy an estate in the mountains of Linyou as a place to flee disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Shenjing befriended the technician Shi Jingzhong, who said the realm would fall into chaos and urged him to buy an estate in the Linyou mountains as a refuge.

sentences.zh: 會慎矜父墓田中草木皆流血，慎矜惡之，以問敬忠。

translations.literal: It happened that in the fields of Shenjing's father's tomb all plants and trees bled; Shenjing was repelled by it and asked Jingzhong.
translations.idiomatic: When plants at his father's tomb bled, Shenjing was troubled and asked Jingzhong.

sentences.zh: 敬忠請禳之，設道場於後園，慎矜退朝，輒裸貫桎梏坐其中。

translations.literal: Jingzhong asked to perform exorcism rites, set up a ritual arena in the rear garden, and whenever Shenjing returned from court he would sit in it naked, pierced through with cangues.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhong offered exorcism rites and set up a ritual ground in the rear garden; Shenjing would return from court and sit there naked in shackles.

sentences.zh: 旬日血止，慎矜德之。

translations.literal: Within ten days the bleeding stopped, and Shenjing was grateful to him.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days the bleeding stopped, and Shenjing was grateful.

sentences.zh: 慎矜有侍婢明珠，色美，敬忠屢目之，慎矜即以遺敬忠，車載過貴妃姊柳氏樓下，姊邀敬忠上樓，求車中美人，敬忠不敢拒。

translations.literal: Shenjing had a serving maid named Bright Pearl, beautiful in appearance; Jingzhong often eyed her, and Shenjing thereupon gave her to Jingzhong; as the cart passed below the tower of the Noble Consort's elder sister of the Liu clan, the sister invited Jingzhong upstairs and asked for the beauty in the cart; Jingzhong did not dare refuse.
translations.idiomatic: Shenjing had a beautiful maid named Bright Pearl; Jingzhong eyed her often, and Shenjing gave her to him; passing the tower of the Noble Consort's Liu sister, she invited Jingzhong up and took the maid—he dared not refuse.

sentences.zh: 明日，姊入宮，以明珠自隨。

translations.literal: The next day the sister entered the palace, taking Bright Pearl with her.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the sister entered the palace with Bright Pearl.

sentences.zh: 上見而異之，問所從來，明珠具以實對。

translations.literal: The emperor saw her and was struck as strange; he asked whence she came, and Bright Pearl answered fully according to fact.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was struck by her and asked her origin; Bright Pearl told the whole truth.

sentences.zh: 上以慎矜與術士為妖法，惡之，含怒未發。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Shenjing practiced sorcery with the technician, hated it and held his anger without yet releasing it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, believing Shenjing practiced sorcery with the technician, hated it and nursed his anger in silence.

sentences.zh: 楊釗以告□，□心喜，因侮慢慎矜；

translations.literal: Yang Zhao reported this to Yue; Yue rejoiced in mind and therefore treated Shenjing with insult and contempt;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhao told Yue, who rejoiced and treated Shenjing with contempt;

sentences.zh: 慎矜怒。

translations.literal: Shenjing was angry.
translations.idiomatic: Shenjing was furious.

sentences.zh: 林甫知□與慎矜有隙，密誘使圖之。

translations.literal: Linfu knew that Yue and Shenjing had a rift and secretly urged him to plot against him.
translations.idiomatic: Linfu, knowing of the rift, secretly urged Yue to plot against him.

sentences.zh: □乃遣人以飛語告「慎矜隋煬帝孫，與凶人往來，家有讖書，謀復祖業。」

translations.literal: Yue then sent a man with whispered slander to report, "Shenjing is a grandson of Emperor Yang of Sui, associates with evil men, keeps prognostic texts in his house, and plots to restore his ancestral enterprise."
translations.idiomatic: Yue sent informers to lodge the accusation that "Shenjing is a grandson of Emperor Yang of Sui, consorting with villains, keeping prognostic texts, and plotting to restore his ancestral enterprise."

sentences.zh: 上大怒，收慎矜繫獄，命刑部、大理與侍御史楊釗、殿中侍御史盧鉉同鞫之。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angry, seized Shenjing and imprisoned him, and ordered the Ministry of Justice, the Court of Judicial Review, Attending Censor Yang Zhao, and Attending Censor Within the Palace Lu Xuan jointly to interrogate him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious, arrested Shenjing, and ordered the Ministry of Justice, Court of Judicial Review, Yang Zhao, and Lu Xuan to interrogate him jointly.

sentences.zh: 太府少卿張瑄，慎矜所薦也，盧鉉誣瑄嘗與慎矜論讖，拷掠百端，瑄不肯答辯。

translations.literal: Zhang Xuan, Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury, had been recommended by Shenjing; Lu Xuan falsely charged that Xuan had once discussed prognostic texts with Shenjing and tortured him in every way, but Xuan would not answer or defend himself.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xuan of the imperial treasury, Shenjing's protégé, was accused of discussing prognostics with him; Lu Xuan tortured him in every way, but Xuan would not confess.

sentences.zh: 乃以木綴其足，使人引其枷柄，向前挽之，身加長數尺，腰細欲絕，眼鼻出血，瑄竟不答。

translations.literal: "They then fastened wood to his feet, had men pull the handle of his cangue and draw it forward; his body was lengthened several chi, his waist grew thin as if to break, blood flowed from eyes and nose—and Xuan in the end did not answer."
translations.idiomatic: "They clamped wood to his feet and pulled his cangue forward until his body stretched several feet, his waist nearly snapped, and blood poured from his eyes and nose—yet Xuan would not speak."

sentences.zh: 又使吉溫捕史敬忠於汝州。

translations.literal: They also had Ji Wen arrest Shi Jingzhong in Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Wen was also sent to arrest Shi Jingzhong in Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 敬忠與溫父素善，溫之幼也，敬忠常抱撫之。

translations.literal: Jingzhong had long been on good terms with Wen's father; when Wen was young, Jingzhong often held and comforted him.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhong had been close to Wen's father and had dandled Wen as a child.

sentences.zh: 及捕獲，溫不與交言，鎖其頸，以布蒙首，驅之馬前。

translations.literal: When he was captured, Wen did not speak with him, locked his neck, covered his head with cloth, and drove him before the horses.
translations.idiomatic: When captured, Wen would not speak to him, locked his neck, hooded his head, and drove him before the horses.

sentences.zh: 至戲水，溫使吏誘之曰：「楊慎矜已款服，惟鬚子一辯，若解人意則生，不然必死，前至溫湯，則求首不獲矣。」

translations.literal: At Xishui, Wen had an officer entice him, saying, "Yang Shenjing has already confessed fully; only the old man's one explanation remains—if you understand what is wanted you live, otherwise you surely die; before you reach the hot springs, you will not even be able to beg for your head."
translations.idiomatic: At Xishui Wen's officer told him, "Shenjing has confessed; only your testimony remains—cooperate and live, resist and die before you even reach the hot springs."

sentences.zh: 敬忠顧謂溫曰：「七郎，求一紙。」

translations.literal: Jingzhong turned and said to Wen, "Seventh Son, I beg one sheet of paper."
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhong turned to Wen and said, "Seventh Son, give me paper."

sentences.zh: 溫陽不應。

translations.literal: Wen pretended not to respond.
translations.idiomatic: Wen feigned not to hear.

sentences.zh: 去溫湯十餘里，敬忠懇請哀切，乃於桑下令答三紙，辯皆如溫意。

translations.literal: More than ten li from the hot springs, Jingzhong pleaded piteously and earnestly; only then, under a mulberry tree, was he made to answer on three sheets, and the defense was entirely as Wen wished.
translations.idiomatic: Ten li from the hot springs Jingzhong begged piteously; under a mulberry tree he wrote three sheets confessing exactly as Wen wished.

sentences.zh: 溫徐謂曰：「丈人且勿怪！」

translations.literal: Wen said slowly, "Elder, do not take offense!"
translations.idiomatic: Wen said gently, "Sir, do not blame me!"

sentences.zh: 因起拜之。

translations.literal: He thereupon rose and bowed to him.
translations.idiomatic: He rose and bowed to him.

sentences.zh: 至會昌，始鞫慎矜，以敬忠為證。

translations.literal: At Huichang they first interrogated Shenjing, using Jingzhong as witness.
translations.idiomatic: At Huichang they interrogated Shenjing, using Jingzhong as witness.

sentences.zh: 慎矜皆引服，惟搜讖書不獲。

translations.literal: Shenjing confessed to everything, but when they searched for prognostic texts they did not recover them.
translations.idiomatic: Shenjing confessed to all charges, but no prognostic texts were found.

sentences.zh: 林甫危之，使盧鉉入長安搜慎矜家，鉉袖讖書入暗中，詬而出曰：「逆賊深藏秘記。」

translations.literal: Linfu was alarmed and had Lu Xuan enter Chang'an to search Shenjing's house; Xuan concealed prognostic texts in his sleeve, entered the darkness, and came out cursing, saying, "The rebel traitor hid secret records."
translations.idiomatic: Linfu, alarmed, had Lu Xuan search Shenjing's house in Chang'an; Xuan slipped prognostic texts from his sleeve and emerged shouting, "The traitor hid secret records."

sentences.zh: 至會昌，以示慎矜。

translations.literal: At Huichang he showed them to Shenjing.
translations.idiomatic: At Huichang he showed them to Shenjing.

sentences.zh: 慎矜歎曰：「吾不蓄讖書，此何從在吾家哉！

translations.literal: Shenjing sighed and said, "I did not keep prognostic texts—how did these come to be in my house!
translations.idiomatic: Shenjing sighed, "I kept no prognostic texts—how did these come to be in my house!

sentences.zh: 吾應死而己。」

translations.literal: I ought to die, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: I deserve to die, that is all."

sentences.zh: 丁酉，賜慎矜及兄少府少監慎餘、洛陽令慎名自盡；

translations.literal: On the day dingyou, Shenjing and his elder brothers Shenyu, Vice Director of the Palace of Supreme Harmony, and Shenming, Magistrate of Luoyang, were granted permission to take their own lives;
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou day Shenjing and his brothers Shenyu and Shenming were permitted to kill themselves;

sentences.zh: 敬忠杖百，妻子皆流嶺南；

translations.literal: Jingzhong received a hundred blows with the staff; wives and children were all exiled to Lingnan;
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhong was beaten a hundred strokes; his family was exiled to Lingnan;

sentences.zh: 瑄杖六十，流臨封，死於會昌。

translations.literal: Xuan received sixty blows and was exiled to Linfeng; he died at Huichang.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan was beaten sixty strokes, exiled to Linfeng, and died at Huichang.

sentences.zh: 嗣虢王巨雖不預謀，坐與敬忠相識，解官，南賓安置。

translations.literal: Heir of Prince Guo Ju, though he had not joined the plot, was charged with knowing Jingzhong, removed from office, and settled at Nanbin.
translations.idiomatic: Heir of Prince Guo Ju, though not part of the plot, was dismissed for knowing Jingzhong and settled at Nanbin.

sentences.zh: 自餘連坐者數十人。

translations.literal: Besides these, several tens suffered joint punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Dozens more suffered joint punishment.

sentences.zh: 慎名聞敕，神色不變，為書別姊；

translations.literal: When Shenming heard the edict, his expression did not change; he wrote a letter of farewell to his elder sister;
