translations.idiomatic: When Shenming heard the edict, his expression did not change; he wrote farewell to his sister;

sentences.zh: 慎餘合掌指天而縊。

translations.literal: Shenyu joined his palms, pointed to Heaven, and hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Shenyu joined his palms toward heaven and hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 三司按王忠嗣，上曰：「吾兒居深宮，安得與外人通謀，此必妄也。

translations.literal: The Three Offices investigated Wang Zhongsi; the emperor said, "My son dwells deep within the palace—how could he plot with outsiders? This must be false.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Offices tried Wang Zhongsi; the emperor said, "My son lives deep in the inner palace—how could he plot with outsiders? This must be false.

sentences.zh: 但劾忠嗣沮撓軍功。」

translations.literal: Only charge Zhongsi with obstructing military achievement."
translations.idiomatic: Charge Zhongsi only with obstructing the campaign."

sentences.zh: 哥舒翰之入朝也，或勸多繼金帛以救忠嗣。

translations.literal: When Geshu Han entered court, some urged him to bring much gold and silk to save Zhongsi.
translations.idiomatic: When Geshu Han came to court, some urged him to bring gold and silk to save Zhongsi.

sentences.zh: 翰曰：「若直道尚存，王公必不冤死；

translations.literal: Han said, "If the straight Way still exists, the lord and prince will surely not die unjustly;
translations.idiomatic: Han said, "If justice still holds in the court, Lord Wang will not die unjustly;

sentences.zh: 如其將喪，多賂何為！」

translations.literal: if it is about to perish, what use are many bribes!"
translations.idiomatic: if it is already lost, what good are bribes!"

sentences.zh: 遂單囊而行。

translations.literal: He thereupon went with only a single satchel.
translations.idiomatic: He went with only a single bag.

sentences.zh: 三司奏忠嗣罪當死。

translations.literal: The Three Offices memorialized that Zhongsi's crime warranted death.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Offices reported that Zhongsi deserved death.

sentences.zh: 翰始遇知於上，力陳忠嗣之冤，且請以己官爵贖忠嗣罪；

translations.literal: Han had just won the emperor's notice; he forcefully set forth Zhongsi's injustice and moreover asked to use his own office and rank to redeem Zhongsi's crime;
translations.idiomatic: Han had just won the emperor's favor; he pleaded Zhongsi's innocence and offered his own rank to redeem him;

sentences.zh: 上起，入禁中，翰叩頭隨之，言與淚俱。

translations.literal: The emperor rose and entered the forbidden precincts; Han kowtowed and followed him, words and tears together.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rose and entered the inner palace; Han kowtowed and followed, speaking through his tears.

sentences.zh: 上感寤，己亥，貶忠嗣漢陽太守。

translations.literal: The emperor was moved and awakened; on the day jihai, Zhongsi was demoted to Prefect of Hanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Moved, the emperor on jihai day demoted Zhongsi to prefect of Hanyang.

sentences.zh: 李林甫屢起大獄，別置推事院於長安。

translations.literal: Li Linfu repeatedly raised great cases and separately established an interrogation office in Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu repeatedly launched great prosecutions and set up a separate interrogation office in Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 以楊釗有掖廷之親，出入禁闥，所言多聽，乃引以為援，擢為御史。

translations.literal: Because Yang Zhao had kinship with the palace women, entering and leaving the forbidden inner gates, and his words were often heeded, Linfu drew him in as support and promoted him to censor.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yang Zhao had palace connections and free access to the inner gates, and the emperor often heeded him, Linfu made him an ally and promoted him to censor.

sentences.zh: 事有微涉東宮者，皆指擿使之奏刻，付羅希奭、吉溫鞫之。

translations.literal: Whenever affairs even slightly touched the Eastern Palace, he would point them out and have Zhao memorialize accusations, handing them to Luo Xiyi and Ji Wen for interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: Anything touching the Eastern Palace he had Zhao accuse, then handed the cases to Luo Xiyi and Ji Wen.

sentences.zh: 釗因得逞其私志，所擠陷誅夷者數百家，皆釗發之。

translations.literal: Zhao thereby fulfilled his private aims; the several hundred households he squeezed, framed, executed, and exterminated were all set in motion by Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao thus fulfilled his private aims; the hundreds of families he destroyed were all brought down by him.

sentences.zh: 幸太子仁孝謹靜，張□、高力士常保護於上前，故林甫終不能間也。

translations.literal: Fortunately the Crown Prince was benevolent, filial, cautious, and quiet; Zhang Ya and Gao Lishi often protected him before the emperor, and therefore Linfu in the end could not drive a wedge.
translations.idiomatic: Fortunately the crown prince was dutiful and cautious; Zhang Ya and Gao Lishi often shielded him at court, and Linfu could never drive a wedge between them.

sentences.zh: 十二月，壬戌，發馮翊、華陰民夫築會昌城，置百司。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day renxu, corvée laborers from Fengyi and Huayin were mobilized to build Huichang city and install the hundred offices.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on renxu day, laborers from Fengyi and Huayin were mobilized to build Huichang city and install the central offices.

sentences.zh: 王公各置第捨，土畝直千金。

translations.literal: Princes and dukes each set up mansions; land per mu was worth a thousand in gold.
translations.idiomatic: Princes and nobles each built mansions there; land sold for a thousand gold per mu.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，上還宮。

translations.literal: On the day guihai, the emperor returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai day the emperor returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，命百官閱天下歲貢物於尚書省，既而悉以車載賜李林甫家。

translations.literal: On the day bingyin, the hundred officials were ordered to review the year's tribute goods from all under Heaven at the Ministry of Revenue; afterward all were loaded on carts and bestowed on Li Linfu's household.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin day officials were ordered to review the year's tribute goods at the Ministry of Revenue; then everything was carted to Li Linfu's house as gifts.

sentences.zh: 上或時不視朝，百司悉集林甫第門，台省為空。

translations.literal: When the emperor sometimes did not hold court, the hundred offices all gathered at Linfu's gate; the secretariat and censorate stood empty.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor skipped court, every office gathered at Linfu's gate and the ministries stood empty.

sentences.zh: 陳希烈雖坐府，無一人入謁者。

translations.literal: Though Chen Xilie sat in his office, not a single person came to call on him.
translations.idiomatic: Though Chen Xilie sat in his office, no one came to call on him.

sentences.zh: 林甫子岫為將作監，頗以滿盈為懼，嘗從林甫游後園，指役夫言於林甫曰：「大人久處鈞軸，怨仇滿天下，一朝禍至，欲為此，得乎？」

translations.literal: Linfu's son Song was Director of Palace Construction and was rather afraid of fullness and overflow; he once followed Linfu touring the rear garden, pointed at the laborers, and said to Linfu, "Father has long stood at the hub of power; enemies and grievances fill all under Heaven. If calamity comes in a morning, would you wish to be like these men—could you?"
translations.idiomatic: Linfu's son Song, director of palace construction, feared their peak had passed; touring the rear garden he pointed at laborers and said, "Father, you have held power so long that enemies fill the realm. If disaster strikes, would you want to end like these men?"

sentences.zh: 林甫不樂曰：「勢已如此，將若之何？」

translations.literal: Linfu, displeased, said, "The situation is already thus—what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Linfu said unhappily, "Things are already thus—what can be done?"

sentences.zh: 先是，宰相皆以德度自處，不事威勢，騶從不過數人，士民或不之避。

translations.literal: Earlier, chancellors all conducted themselves by virtue and magnanimity, did not cultivate intimidating power, and their mounted escorts did not exceed several men; scholars and commoners sometimes did not avoid them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier chancellors conducted themselves with virtue and restraint, cultivated no intimidating display, and kept only a few mounted escorts; commoners sometimes did not even step aside for them.

sentences.zh: 林甫自以多結怨，常虞刺客，出則步騎百餘人為左右翼，金吾靜街，前驅在數百步外，公卿走避；

translations.literal: Linfu, considering that he had made many enmities, constantly feared assassins; when he went out, more than a hundred foot soldiers and horsemen formed his left and right wings, the Golden Guard cleared the streets, and his vanguard was several hundred paces ahead; dukes and ministers fled to avoid him;
translations.idiomatic: Linfu, knowing he had made many enemies, constantly feared assassins; when he went out, more than a hundred guards flanked him, the Golden Guard cleared the streets, and his vanguard rode hundreds of paces ahead; nobles fled to avoid him;

sentences.zh: 居則重關復壁，以石甃地，牆中置板，如防大敵，一夕屢徙床，雖家人莫知其處。

translations.literal: at home he had double gates and layered walls, paved the ground with stone, set boards within the walls as if guarding against a great enemy, and in one night moved his bed many times—even his household did not know where he was.
translations.idiomatic: at home he kept double gates and layered walls, paved the floors with stone, set boards in the walls as against a great enemy, and moved his bed many times in a single night—even his family did not know where he slept.

sentences.zh: 宰相騶從之盛，自林甫始。

translations.literal: The grandeur of chancellors' mounted escorts began with Linfu.
translations.idiomatic: The grandeur of a chancellor's escort began with Linfu.

sentences.zh: 初，將軍高仙芝，本高麗人，從軍安西。

translations.literal: Earlier, General Gao Xianzhi was originally a man of Goguryeo and followed the army in Anxi.
translations.idiomatic: General Gao Xianzhi was originally from Goguryeo and had joined the army in Anxi.

sentences.zh: 仙芝驍勇，善騎射。

translations.literal: Xianzhi was fierce and brave and skilled in mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi was fierce and skilled in mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 節度使夫蒙靈察屢薦至安西副都護、都知兵馬使，充四鎮節度副使。

translations.literal: Military Commissioner Fumeng Lingcha repeatedly recommended him until he became Anxi Vice Protector-General, overall commander of military affairs, and filled the post of deputy military commissioner of the Four Garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioner Fumeng Lingcha repeatedly promoted him until he became Anxi vice protector-general, overall commander of military affairs, and deputy commissioner of the Four Garrisons.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃以女妻小勃律王，及其旁二十餘國，皆附吐蕃，貢獻不入；

translations.literal: Tibet gave a daughter in marriage to the king of Little Bolü, and together with more than twenty states beside it, all attached themselves to Tibet and sent no tribute inward;
translations.idiomatic: Tibet married a princess to the king of Little Bolü, and more than twenty neighboring states followed Tibet and sent no tribute to Tang;

sentences.zh: 前後節度使討之，皆不能克。

translations.literal: former and later military commissioners campaigned against them but none could overcome them.
translations.idiomatic: successive commissioners had campaigned against them without success.

sentences.zh: 制以仙芝為行營節度使，將萬騎討之。

translations.literal: By imperial order Xianzhi was made campaign military commissioner and led ten thousand horsemen to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: The court made Xianzhi campaign commissioner and sent him with ten thousand horsemen.

sentences.zh: 自安西行百餘日，乃至特勒滿川，分軍為三道，期以七月十三日會吐蕃連雲堡下。

translations.literal: From Anxi he marched more than a hundred days until he reached the Teliman River, divided the army into three routes, and set the thirteenth day of the seventh month to converge below Tibet's Lianyun Fortress.
translations.idiomatic: From Anxi he marched more than a hundred days to the Teliman River, divided his army into three columns, and set the thirteenth day of the seventh month to converge below Tibet's Lianyun Fortress.

sentences.zh: 有兵近萬人，不意唐兵猝至，大驚，依山拒戰，砲櫑如雨。

translations.literal: They had nearly ten thousand troops; not expecting Tang troops to arrive suddenly, they were greatly alarmed, relied on the mountains to resist battle, and projectiles fell like rain.
translations.idiomatic: Nearly ten thousand defenders, surprised by the sudden Tang arrival, fought from the mountains while projectiles rained down.

sentences.zh: 仙芝以郎將高陵李嗣業為陌刀將，令之曰：「不及日中，決須破虜！」

translations.literal: Xianzhi made Lang Commander Li Siye of Gaoling commander of the long-handled blades and ordered him, saying, "Before midday you must decisively break the enemy!"
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi made Li Siye of Gaoling commander of the long-handled blades and ordered, "Break the enemy before noon!"

sentences.zh: 嗣業執一旗，引陌刀緣險先登力戰，自辰至巳，大破之，斬首五千級，捕虜千餘人，餘皆逃潰。

translations.literal: Siye took one banner, led the long-handled blades along the perilous ground to climb first and fight with force; from the chen hour to the si hour he broke them greatly, beheaded five thousand, captured more than a thousand prisoners, and the rest all fled in rout.
translations.idiomatic: Siye seized a banner and led the blade troops up the dangerous slope to attack first; from mid-morning to late morning he routed them, took five thousand heads and more than a thousand prisoners, and the rest fled.

sentences.zh: 中使邊令誠以入虜境已深，懼不敢進；

translations.literal: Palace Envoy Bian Lingcheng, because they had already entered deep into enemy territory, was afraid and did not dare advance;
translations.idiomatic: Palace envoy Bian Lingcheng, fearing they had penetrated too deep, would not advance;

sentences.zh: 仙芝乃使令誠以羸弱三千守期城，復進。

translations.literal: Xianzhi then had Lingcheng hold Qicheng with three thousand weak troops and advanced again.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi left Lingcheng with three thousand weak troops to hold Qicheng and advanced again.

sentences.zh: 三日，至坦駒嶺，下峻阪四十餘里，前有阿弩越城。

translations.literal: On the third day they reached Tanju Ridge; below was a steep slope of more than forty li, and ahead lay Anuyue City.
translations.idiomatic: On the third day they reached Tanju Ridge, with a steep descent of more than forty li ahead and Anuyue City beyond.

sentences.zh: 仙芝恐士卒憚險，不肯下，先令人胡服詐為阿弩越城守者迎降，云：「阿弩越赤心歸唐，娑夷水籐橋已斫斷矣。」

translations.literal: Xianzhi feared the soldiers would dread the peril and refuse to descend; he first had men in barbarian dress falsely pose as defenders of Anuyue City coming to welcome surrender, saying, "Anuyue is loyal at heart to Tang; the vine bridge over the Suoyi water has already been cut down."
translations.idiomatic: Fearing his men would refuse the descent, Xianzhi sent men in barbarian dress to pose as Anuyue defenders welcoming surrender, saying, "Anuyue is loyal to Tang; the vine bridge over the Suoyi River has been cut."

sentences.zh: 娑夷，即弱水也，其水不能勝草芥。

translations.literal: Suoyi is the Weak Water; its waters cannot bear even a blade of grass.
translations.idiomatic: The Suoyi is the Weak Water, which cannot bear even a blade of grass.

sentences.zh: 籐橋者，通吐蕃之路也。

translations.literal: The vine bridge was the road connecting to Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: The vine bridge was the route to Tibet.

sentences.zh: 仙芝陽喜，士卒乃下。

translations.literal: Xianzhi feigned joy, and the soldiers then descended.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi feigned delight, and the soldiers descended.

sentences.zh: 又三日，阿弩越城迎者果至。

translations.literal: After three more days, the welcomers from Anuyue City indeed arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later the welcomers from Anuyue City arrived as promised.

sentences.zh: 明日，仙芝入阿弩越城，遣將軍席元慶將千騎前行，謂曰：「小勃律聞大軍至，其君臣百姓必走山谷，弟呼出，取繒帛稱敕賜之，大臣至，盡縛之以待我。」

translations.literal: The next day Xianzhi entered Anuyue City and sent General Xi Yuanqing ahead with a thousand horsemen, saying, "When Little Bolü hears the great army has come, its ruler, ministers, and common people will surely flee into the valleys. Younger brother, call them out, take silk and claim an imperial edict to bestow it; when the ministers arrive, bind them all and wait for me."
translations.idiomatic: The next day Xianzhi entered Anuyue City and sent General Xi Yuanqing ahead with a thousand horsemen, saying, "When Little Bolü hears we are coming, the court and people will flee to the hills. Call them out, give silk in the emperor's name, and bind every minister who comes—hold them for me."

sentences.zh: 元慶如其言，悉縛諸大臣。

translations.literal: Yuanqing did as he said and bound all the ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqing did as told and bound all the ministers.

sentences.zh: 王及吐蕃公主逃入石窟，取不可得，仙芝至，斬其附吐蕃者大臣數人。

translations.literal: The king and the Tibetan princess fled into a stone cave and could not be taken; when Xianzhi arrived, he beheaded several ministers who had attached themselves to Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: The king and the Tibetan princess fled into a cave and could not be taken; when Xianzhi arrived he beheaded several ministers who had sided with Tibet.

sentences.zh: 籐橋去城猶六十里，仙芝急遣元慶往斫之，甫畢，吐蕃兵大至，已無及矣。

translations.literal: The vine bridge was still sixty li from the city; Xianzhi urgently sent Yuanqing to cut it down, and just as he finished, Tibetan troops arrived in great numbers—it was already too late.
translations.idiomatic: The vine bridge lay sixty li away; Xianzhi urgently sent Yuanqing to cut it, but just as he finished, Tibetan troops arrived in force—it was too late.

sentences.zh: 籐橋闊盡一矢，力修之，期年乃成。

translations.literal: The vine bridge spanned a full arrow-shot in width; they strained to repair it, and only after a full year was it completed.
translations.idiomatic: The bridge spanned a full arrow-shot; they strained to repair it, and it took a full year to finish.

sentences.zh: 八月，仙芝虜小勃律王及吐蕃公主而還。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Xianzhi captured the king of Little Bolü and the Tibetan princess and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Xianzhi captured the king of Little Bolü and the Tibetan princess and returned.

sentences.zh: 九月，至連雲堡，與邊令誠俱。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he reached Lianyun Fortress, together with Bian Lingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he reached Lianyun Fortress with Bian Lingcheng.

sentences.zh: 月末，至播密川，遣使奏狀。

translations.literal: At month's end he reached the Bomi River and sent envoys to memorialize the situation.
translations.idiomatic: At month's end he reached the Bomi River and sent a victory report.

sentences.zh: 至河西，夫蒙靈察怒仙芝不先言己而遽發奏，一不迎勞，罵仙芝曰：「啖狗糞高麗奴！

translations.literal: When he reached Hexi, Fumeng Lingcha was angry that Xianzhi had not spoken to him first but had hurriedly sent in his memorial; he did not welcome or comfort him at all and cursed Xianzhi, saying, "Dog-dung-eating Goguryeo slave!
translations.idiomatic: At Hexi, Fumeng Lingcha was furious that Xianzhi had reported victory without telling him first; he did not welcome him and cursed, "Dog-shit-eating Goguryeo slave!

sentences.zh: 汝官皆困誰得，而不待我處分，擅奏捷書！

translations.literal: Every office you hold—through whose entanglement did you get them—and yet you did not await my disposition and on your own memorialized a victory report!
translations.idiomatic: Who got you every office you hold—and you did not wait for my orders before sending in your victory report!

sentences.zh: 高麗奴！

translations.literal: Goguryeo slave!
translations.idiomatic: Goguryeo slave!

sentences.zh: 汝罪當斬，但以汝新有功不忍耳！」

translations.literal: Your crime deserves decapitation, but only because you have fresh achievement I cannot bear to do it!"
translations.idiomatic: Your crime deserves death, but I spare you only because of your fresh achievement!"

sentences.zh: 仙芝但謝罪。

translations.literal: Xianzhi only apologized for his crime.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi could only apologize.

sentences.zh: 邊令誠奏仙芝深入萬里，立奇功，今旦夕憂死。

translations.literal: Bian Lingcheng memorialized that Xianzhi had penetrated ten thousand li, achieved a strange and great merit, and now from morning to evening feared death.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Lingcheng memorialized that Xianzhi had marched ten thousand li, won a great victory, and now feared for his life day and night.
